epics.title: E02 — Core Character Controller
epics.description:
## Outcome
Movement, camera, jumping, climbing, stance, interaction, targeting and animation hooks feel excellent and responsive on keyboard + mouse (gamepad second). All movement rules live in src/sim as a deterministic kinematic controller driven by abstract input actions, so replays, AI and tests share the exact same rules the player feels.
## Scope
- In: Remappable input action layer (KB/M, then gamepad) producing deterministic per-tick action frames
- In: Kinematic third-person controller: walk/run/sprint, jump, gravity, slopes, steps, crouch stance
- In: Traversal verbs: ledge mantle/grab, climbable surfaces, wading/swimming, walking on ice, external impulses
- In: Third-person camera with collision, lock-on targeting, contextual interact/focus verb, carry/push objects
- In: Animation state + footstep event hooks, controller tuning data, latency and determinism verification
- Out: Combat moves (attack/block/parry/dodge) — see mw-e04 (e04-melee-core)
- Out: Bow aiming camera specifics — see mw-e05 (e05-bow-core)
- Out: Stealth visibility/noise scoring — see mw-e09 (consumes stance and footstep hooks from this epic)
- Out: Final character models and animation clips — see mw-e37
## Exit criteria
- Input-to-motion latency ≤ 100 ms (p95) measured by Playwright on the reference machine; controller sim cost ≤ 0.3 ms per tick.
- A recorded 60 s traversal replay (run, jump, mantle, climb, crouch, swim) reproduces an identical sim state hash on every CI run.
- All controller rules in src/sim at 100% coverage; every tuning value lives in schema-validated content data.
- A playtester can traverse the greybox traversal course (e00-greybox-testbed) using only KB/M and, separately, only a gamepad.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 Input-to-motion latency ≤ 100 ms (p95) measured by Playwright on the reference machine; controller sim cost ≤ 0.3 ms per tick.
- EC-2 A recorded 60 s traversal replay (run, jump, mantle, climb, crouch, swim) reproduces an identical sim state hash on every CI run.
- EC-3 All controller rules in src/sim at 100% coverage; every tuning value lives in schema-validated content data.
- EC-4 A playtester can traverse the greybox traversal course (e00-greybox-testbed) using only KB/M and, separately, only a gamepad.

epics.title: E03 — Systemic Interaction Engine
epics.description:
## Outcome
Doors, switches, movable objects, breakables, fire, water, ice, electricity, gas, light, physics and triggers form one reusable, property-based world simulation. Nothing is scripted pairwise: objects declare properties (flammable, wet, frozen, conductive, weight, fragile, climbable, liftable, hideable, reflective…) and elements propagate by rules over those properties, so a spell, an arrow, a torch, a creature and a puzzle all touch the same systems. This is the architectural heart of "Wait… I can do that?".
## Scope
- In: Typed world-property components + data-defined material presets
- In: A single stimulus API that spells, arrows, weapons, creatures and environment all use to inject heat, water, cold, charge, force, gas and light
- In: Element propagation rules: fire/heat, water/wetness, freezing/melting, electricity, gas, wind/force
- In: Light field (queryable light level per position), extinguishable/ignitable light sources, redirectable light beams
- In: Physics objects (movable, throwable, stackable, breakable, liftable/levitatable, buoyant), ropes/supports
- In: Doors, locks, levers, pressure plates, shootable mechanisms, trigger volumes and data-wired signal logic
- In: Hiding places and containers; climbable surface markup; actor participation in properties
- In: Interaction-matrix property-test harness, emergence scenario replays, debug overlays and perf budgets
- Out: Specific spells/arrows/abilities — see mw-e06/e08, mw-e05, mw-e10 (they emit stimuli through this epic)
- Out: Stealth scoring and AI perception — see mw-e09/mw-e11 (they query the light field and receive world noise events)
- Out: Puzzle authoring and solvability — see mw-e15
- Out: Persistence of world changes — see mw-e27
## Exit criteria
- No code path in src/sim or src/content references a pair of specific object types to produce an interaction; a lint/grep check in CI enforces that interaction rules read only properties.
- The interaction-matrix harness property-tests every element × property combination and runs in CI in ≤ 60 s.
- The greybox "chaos room" scenario library (≥ 12 emergent combos) replays deterministically to identical state hashes.
- Element simulation costs ≤ 2.0 ms per tick p95 with 2,000 active cells on the reference machine.
- src/sim portions at 100% coverage.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 No code path in src/sim or src/content references a pair of specific object types to produce an interaction; a lint/grep check in CI enforces that interaction rules read only properties.
- EC-2 The interaction-matrix harness property-tests every element × property combination and runs in CI in ≤ 60 s.
- EC-3 The greybox "chaos room" scenario library (≥ 12 emergent combos) replays deterministically to identical state hashes.
- EC-4 Element simulation costs ≤ 2.0 ms per tick p95 with 2,000 active cells on the reference machine.
- EC-5 src/sim portions at 100% coverage.

epics.title: E15 — Puzzle Framework
epics.description:
## Outcome
Designers compose systemic puzzles from reusable world objects and data — not custom code. A puzzle is a data file naming world entities, a goal condition over live properties and world facts, declared solutions per capability set, and reset/hint policies. Tooling proves each declared solution is reachable, detects softlocks, and reports which classes can solve each puzzle, so "several solutions" is verified rather than hoped for.
## Scope
- In: Zod puzzle schema, goal-condition language over properties + world facts, puzzle runtime (e15-puzzle-kit)
- In: Prefab puzzle pieces built purely from e03 components (statues, mirrors, braziers, basins, counterweights…)
- In: Ordered/timed/sound-clue mechanisms, softlock guards and diegetic resets, escalating diegetic hints
- In: Headless solvability validator, multi-solution class-coverage audit in CI, puzzle inspector tool
- In: Reference greybox puzzles covering the constitution examples, puzzle telemetry events
- Out: Final dungeon puzzle content — see mw-e26 / mw-e24 (they author puzzles with this kit)
- Out: Underlying element/mechanism simulation — see mw-e03
- Out: Separate minigames (lockpicking UI) — see mw-e10
## Exit criteria
- A designer can author a new two-solution puzzle using only data + prefabs, with zero new TypeScript, and it passes the solvability validator.
- CI fails if any puzzle tagged mvp has fewer than 2 validated solutions or any reachable softlock without a recovery policy.
- Six reference greybox puzzles (light redirect, freezing water, weighted plates, statues, darkness navigation, sound following) are replay-tested end to end.
- Puzzle runtime and validator logic in src/sim/src/tools meet coverage policy (100% / ≥ 90%).
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 A designer can author a new two-solution puzzle using only data + prefabs, with zero new TypeScript, and it passes the solvability validator.
- EC-2 CI fails if any puzzle tagged mvp has fewer than 2 validated solutions or any reachable softlock without a recovery policy.
- EC-3 Six reference greybox puzzles (light redirect, freezing water, weighted plates, statues, darkness navigation, sound following) are replay-tested end to end.
- EC-4 Puzzle runtime and validator logic in src/sim/src/tools meet coverage policy (100% / ≥ 90%).

epics.title: E27 — Dynamic World State
epics.description:
## Outcome
Meaningful actions persist: doors opened, walls smashed, ropes burned, chests looted, creatures befriended, treasures stolen, characters helped. A typed, deterministic world-fact store plus per-entity deltas against authored baselines captures the world as the player left it and flows through e30 save serialization. Quests, dialogue, puzzles and level variants all read the same facts.
## Scope
- In: Typed world-fact store (e27-world-state-store) with registry, change events and deterministic ordering
- In: Entity delta persistence (moved/broken/burned/looted/dead) relative to authored level baselines
- In: Save/load integration and migrations via e30, fact query/condition API shared by quests/dialogue/puzzles
- In: Persistence policies (permanent/rest-reset/transient), offscreen elapsed-time catch-up, fact-gated world variants
- In: Ownership/theft facts, debug inspector, size/perf budgets
- Out: Save file format, IndexedDB storage and migration framework — see e30-save-serialization
- Out: Quest and dialogue runtimes — see e23-quest-runtime, e22-dialogue-runtime (they consume facts)
- Out: Crime/witness reactions — see mw-e11 / mw-e10
## Exit criteria
- Smashing a wall, burning a rope bridge, looting a chest and befriending a creature, then save → reload (and full browser restart) restores all four exactly (e2e).
- World state for 10,000 facts + 5,000 entity deltas serializes in ≤ 50 ms and ≤ 1 MB compressed.
- Every fact written at runtime is declared in the content fact registry; undeclared writes fail tests.
- src/sim world-state code and save integration at 100% coverage with round-trip and migration tests.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 Smashing a wall, burning a rope bridge, looting a chest and befriending a creature, then save → reload (and full browser restart) restores all four exactly (e2e).
- EC-2 World state for 10,000 facts + 5,000 entity deltas serializes in ≤ 50 ms and ≤ 1 MB compressed.
- EC-3 Every fact written at runtime is declared in the content fact registry; undeclared writes fail tests.
- EC-4 src/sim world-state code and save integration at 100% coverage with round-trip and migration tests.

items.title: Map remappable KB/M input to deterministic per-tick action frames
items.description:
## Why
Keyboard + mouse comes first (Technical constitution). Everything downstream — controller, combat, spells, replays, AI-driven test bots — must consume abstract actions, not raw keys, so the sim stays deterministic and remapping is free.
## What
As a player, I want every game action bound to remappable keys and mouse buttons so that I can play comfortably and the game reacts identically every time.

An action map (Move, Look, Jump, Sprint, Crouch, Interact, LockOn, CycleTarget, PrimaryAttack, SecondaryAttack, Ability1–4, Inventory, Pause, …) turns DOM input into an immutable ActionFrame sampled once per fixed sim tick (digital buttons with pressed/held/released edges, analog move vector, look delta). The sim only ever sees ActionFrames.
## Scope
- In: Action registry (data-defined), default KB/M bindings, runtime rebinding API with conflict detection
- In: ActionFrame sampling aligned to e00-sim-core ticks; pointer lock handling
- In: Bindings persisted through the settings store
- Out: Gamepad — see e02-input-gamepad
- Out: Remapping UI screen — see mw-e31 (uses this API)
## Notes
ActionFrame is plain data so e00-replay-harness can record/replay it verbatim. Keep raw DOM handling in src/game; the frame type lives in src/sim. Related: mw-e31 accessibility remapping UI.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the default binding set, when W and Space are pressed in the same tick, then the ActionFrame contains move=(0,1) and jump.pressed=true, and on the next tick jump.held=true, jump.pressed=false.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a rebind of Jump to F, when F is pressed, then Jump fires and Space no longer does.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a rebind that collides with an existing binding in the same context, when applied, then the API returns a conflict listing both actions and leaves bindings unchanged.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a key pressed and released within a single tick (between samples), when the frame is sampled, then pressed=true and released=true are both reported so taps are never lost.
- AC-5 [integration] Given pointer lock is lost (Esc / window blur), when the next frame is sampled, then all held actions are released and look delta is zero (no stuck keys).
- AC-6 [integration] Given bindings saved via e31-settings-framework, when the page reloads, then custom bindings are restored.

items.title: Move the player with a deterministic third-person kinematic controller
items.description:
## Why
Movement is the verb the player uses every second; if it feels mushy nothing else matters. Keeping it in src/sim means replays, AI and tests share the exact rules the player feels.
## What
As a player, I want tight, weighty walk/run/sprint, jump and crouch movement so that exploring the world feels excellent.

A kinematic capsule controller in src/sim consumes ActionFrames and the camera yaw, resolves collisions against the physics world, handles slopes, steps, ground snapping, jump arcs, coyote time and jump buffering, and exposes a movement state (grounded/airborne/crouched/sprinting) plus the capsule shape (crouch lowers it). Climb/traverse extension points are defined here and filled in by later items.
## Scope
- In: Walk/run/sprint with accel/decel curves, air control, gravity, jump, coyote time (≤ 120 ms), jump buffer (≤ 150 ms)
- In: Slope limit, step-up, ground snapping, moving-platform carry
- In: Crouch stance with reduced capsule and uncrouch obstruction check
- In: Traversal hook interface (climb, mantle, swim) for later items
- Out: Ledges/climbing — see e02-ledge-mantle, e02-climb-surfaces
- Out: Stance stealth modifiers — see e02-stance-profiles
- Out: Dodge roll — see e04-melee-core
## Notes
Starting numbers (all in content data, tunable): run 5.0 m/s, sprint 7.5 m/s, crouch 2.2 m/s, reach max speed in 0.15 s, stop in 0.10 s, jump apex 1.2 m, step height 0.35 m, slope limit 45°. Physics queries go through a thin collision-world interface so the sim is unit-testable with a fake world; the Rapier implementation follows e00-engine-decision.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a grounded player at rest on flat ground, when move=(0,1) is held, then speed reaches 5.0 m/s ± 0.05 within 0.15 s and releasing stops the player within 0.10 s.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a grounded player, when jump is pressed, then apex height is 1.2 m ± 0.02 and the player lands on the same tick count on every run.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the player walked off a ledge 100 ms ago, when jump is pressed, then the jump executes (coyote time); at 130 ms it does not.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a 0.30 m step, when walking into it, then the player steps up without losing more than 10% speed; given a 0.40 m step, then the player is blocked.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a 50° slope, when walking up it, then the player slides back down and cannot ascend; a 40° slope is climbable at ≥ 80% speed.
- AC-6 [unit] Given a crouched player under a 1.2 m ceiling, when crouch is released, then the player stays crouched until the obstruction clears (edge).
- AC-7 [integration] Given the greybox traversal course and a recorded input log, when replayed twice, then final sim state hashes are identical.

items.title: Move controller tuning values into schema-validated content data
items.description:
## Why
Feel is found by iteration (rapid iteration is a technical pillar). Designers must tune speeds, jump arcs and camera feel live without code changes.
## What
Controller and camera parameters live in a zod-validated content file (content/controller/*.json) with per-class overrides (e.g. thief crouch faster, knight in heavy armor slower). The debug console can live-edit values and dump the modified file.
## Scope
- In: Schema + default file + per-class override merge
- In: Debug console commands: ctl.get, ctl.set, ctl.dump
- In: Hot reload in dev
- Out: Armor weight effects on movement — see mw-e17 (supplies modifiers)
## Notes
Values documented with units in the schema description fields.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the controller data file, when validated, then every numeric field has declared units and range and the default file passes.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a class override that sets only crouchSpeed, when merged, then all other values come from the base profile.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an out-of-range value (negative gravity), when loaded, then validation fails with the field path in the error.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the debug console, when ctl.set runSpeed 6 is executed, then the next tick uses 6.0 m/s and ctl.dump outputs a valid file.

items.title: Follow the player with a colliding, orbiting third-person camera
items.description:
## Why
A camera that clips into walls or loses the player breaks exploration and combat. Camera options are also an accessibility concern (E31).
## What
As a player, I want a smooth third-person camera I control with the mouse so that I can always see my character and surroundings.

Orbit camera with shoulder offset, pitch limits, sensitivity/invert options, zoom, collision pull-in against level geometry (never inside walls), and smooth recovery. Camera yaw feeds the controller as data so movement is camera-relative but still deterministic.
## Scope
- In: Orbit + shoulder offset, pitch clamp (-70°..+60°), zoom 2–6 m, sensitivity + invert Y
- In: Sphere-cast collision pull-in, recovery easing, transparency fade of occluders near the camera
- In: Camera yaw injected into ActionFrame for camera-relative movement
- Out: Lock-on framing — see e02-lock-on
- Out: Bow aim camera — see e05-bow-core
- Out: Motion sickness options UI — see mw-e31
## Notes
Camera lives in src/game/src/render (presentation), but the yaw consumed by sim is quantised into the ActionFrame so replays are exact. Default FOV 70°.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given pitch input beyond the clamp, when applied, then pitch stays within -70°..+60°.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a wall between the ideal camera position and the player, when resolved, then the camera is placed ≥ 0.2 m in front of the wall on the same frame (no clipping frame).
- AC-3 [unit] Given the occluder disappears, when recovering, then the camera returns to the ideal distance over 0.3 s ± 0.05 without overshoot.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the camera yaw is 90°, when move=(0,1), then the player moves along the camera forward vector (camera-relative).
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed, when the Playwright bot walks the player along a narrow corridor with pillars, then no rendered frame has the near plane inside geometry (depth probe) and there are no console errors.
- AC-6 [manual] Given a playtest, when 3 testers orbit and move for 5 minutes, then none report nausea or losing sight of the character.

items.title: Focus and interact with world objects via contextual prompts
items.description:
## Why
The world rewards curiosity: bookshelves, levers, chests, bodies, statues must all respond to one consistent interact verb.
## What
As a player, I want to look at an object and press Interact to use it so that exploring feels natural and I always know what I can do.

Objects expose interaction affordances (open, pull, pick up, read, search, hide, climb, talk…) declared as components. A focus selector in src/sim scores candidates by distance, view angle and line of sight and picks one focus target; the UI shows a contextual prompt. Affordances may be gated by class/capability or item (locked → "Pick lock" for thief, "Unlock" with key).
## Scope
- In: Interactable component with affordance list, range, required capability/item predicate
- In: Deterministic focus scoring + LOS check, hysteresis to prevent flicker
- In: Interaction event dispatch to owning systems; contextual prompt model for UI (text + binding glyph)
- In: Hold-to-interact durations
- Out: Prompt visuals — see mw-e31/ui work
- Out: Specific affordances (doors, containers) — see e03-doors-locks-switches, e03-hiding-containers
## Notes
Scoring: score = w_d*(1 - d/range) + w_a*cos(angle); range default 2.5 m, max angle 45°. Ties broken by entity id for determinism. Unavailable affordances are still shown greyed with the reason (e.g. "Locked — needs Iron Key") to hint at alternate routes.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given two interactables at 1.0 m (30° off-axis) and 2.0 m (straight ahead), when focus is computed, then the selection matches the documented scoring and is identical across runs.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an interactable behind a wall within range, when focus is computed, then it is not selected (LOS).
- AC-3 [unit] Given focus on A and a new candidate B scoring within 10% of A, when computed, then focus stays on A (hysteresis).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a locked door and a player without the key or lockpicking capability, when focused, then the prompt shows the affordance as unavailable with the reason and Interact dispatches nothing.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a hold-to-interact affordance (1.0 s), when Interact is released at 0.8 s, then the interaction is cancelled and no event fires.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed, when the bot faces a lever and presses Interact, then the lever event fires and the prompt DOM element displays the bound key.

items.title: Drive character animation from sim locomotion state and events
items.description:
## Why
Animation must reflect the sim exactly (no sliding feet, no "floaty" jumps) without leaking renderer concerns into the sim.
## What
As a developer, I want the sim to publish a locomotion state snapshot and discrete animation events so that any renderer/animation set can play matching clips.

The sim emits: locomotion state (idle/walk/run/sprint/crouch/airborne/landing/climb/mantle/swim), normalised speed, turn rate, and events (jumpStart, land{impactSpeed}, footstep{foot}, mantleStart, ledgeGrab). src/game maps these to an animation state machine on grey-box/Mixamo rigs.
## Scope
- In: LocomotionSnapshot type + event stream in sim
- In: Blend-tree driver in render using speed/turn rate; root motion NOT authoritative
- In: Grey-box capsule-man placeholder rig
- Out: Combat animation layers — see e04-melee-core
- Out: Final character rigs — see e37-3d-pipeline-decision
## Notes
Footstep events are produced from sim stride distance, not from animation curves, so they stay deterministic (consumed by e02-footstep-events).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a player accelerating from idle to run, when snapshots are sampled, then state transitions idle→walk→run occur at documented speed thresholds (0.2, 2.5 m/s).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a fall of 3 m, when landing, then exactly one land event fires with impactSpeed within ±2% of the analytic value.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the player is pushed sideways while idle (external impulse), when sampled, then state is not "walk" unless input is present (no false locomotion).
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed, when the bot runs and jumps, then the placeholder rig plays run and jump clips (animation state probe) and there are no console errors.
- AC-5 [perf] Given 20 animated characters in the greybox scene, when running for 30 s, then animation update cost ≤ 1.0 ms per frame p95 on the reference machine (High).

items.title: Lock controller determinism with golden replay tests in CI
items.description:
## Why
Determinism is a constitution-level technical goal; controller regressions are silent and must be caught automatically.
## What
Record golden input logs on the greybox traversal course (run, jump, crouch, slopes, steps, later mantle/climb/swim) and assert final and periodic state hashes in CI. Provide a script to re-bless goldens intentionally with a diff report.
## Scope
- In: 3 golden logs (basic, slopes/steps, stress with rapid direction changes)
- In: Periodic hash checkpoints every 60 ticks to localise divergence
- In: Re-bless script with human-readable diff
- Out: Replay harness itself — see e00-replay-harness
## Notes
Extend goldens as traversal items land (each traversal item adds a clip).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given each golden log, when replayed in CI, then every checkpoint hash matches the committed golden.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a deliberate 1% change to runSpeed, when replayed, then the test fails and reports the first divergent checkpoint tick.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a log recorded at a different frame rate (30 vs 144 Hz render), when replayed, then sim hashes are identical (render rate independence).

items.title: Enforce input latency and controller cost budgets in the perf suite
items.description:
## Why
"Responsive" must be a number. The contract requires numeric feel targets and perf budgets on the reference machine.
## What
Add Playwright perf tests measuring input-to-motion latency (synthetic key event timestamp → first rendered frame where the player transform changed) and controller + camera CPU cost per tick; wire into e32 budgets.
## Scope
- In: Latency probe hook in dev builds only
- In: Budgets: input-to-motion ≤ 100 ms p95 (target ≤ 50 ms), controller sim ≤ 0.3 ms/tick p95, camera ≤ 0.2 ms/frame p95
- Out: General frame-time budgets — see e32-perf-budgets
## Notes
Latency probe must be stripped from production bundles (check bundle for the probe symbol).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the greybox testbed on the reference machine (High), when 50 synthetic move key presses are measured, then input-to-motion latency is ≤ 100 ms at p95.
- AC-2 [perf] Given 60 s of scripted traversal, when profiled, then controller sim cost ≤ 0.3 ms per tick p95 and camera ≤ 0.2 ms per frame p95.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a production build, when the bundle is scanned, then the latency probe symbol is absent.
- AC-4 [perf] Given a simulated 30 fps render (low preset worst case), when measured, then input-to-motion latency is ≤ 133 ms p95 (edge).

items.title: Support gamepad input with deadzones and remappable bindings
items.description:
## Why
Gamepad is second after KB/M (Technical constitution). Action RPG combat is commonly played on a pad.
## What
As a player, I want to plug in a standard gamepad and play with sensible defaults so that I can play from the couch.

Gamepad API polling mapped into the same ActionFrame: radial deadzone, response curve, right-stick look with acceleration, default standard-mapping bindings, rebinding, hot-plug, and last-used-device prompt glyph switching.
## Scope
- In: Standard mapping (Xbox/PS layouts) defaults, radial deadzone 0.15 configurable, look curve
- In: Hot-plug connect/disconnect, device-switch detection for prompt glyphs
- Out: Aim assist — see e05-bow-core / e02-lock-on
- Out: Haptics — P3 later
## Notes
Browser Gamepad API differs across Chrome/Firefox/Safari; test standard mapping only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given stick input magnitude 0.10, when processed with deadzone 0.15, then move vector is (0,0); at magnitude 1.0 it is length 1.0.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the stick at magnitude 0.575 (midway between deadzone and full), when processed, then output magnitude is 0.5 ± 0.01 (rescaled radial deadzone).
- AC-3 [unit] Given both KB and gamepad produce move input in one tick, when merged, then the larger-magnitude vector wins and length never exceeds 1.0.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a gamepad disconnects mid-sprint, when the next frame is sampled, then all gamepad-held actions release and the game pauses per settings.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the last input came from the gamepad, when the interact prompt renders, then it shows the gamepad glyph.

items.title: Expose stance and movement profiles for stealth noise and visibility
items.description:
## Why
Stealth cannot be crouching + an eye icon: stance and speed must feed visibility and noise as numbers (Thief constitution).
## What
As a thief, I want my stance and speed to meaningfully change how visible and loud I am so that careful movement is rewarded.

The controller publishes a MovementProfile each tick: stance (standing/crouched), gait (still/walk/run/sprint), silhouette height, and normalised noise and visibility multipliers from data. A "slow walk" modifier (hold key / light stick) gives the quietest gait.
## Scope
- In: MovementProfile type and data table per stance × gait
- In: Slow-walk modifier action
- In: Armor/encumbrance multiplier hook (value supplied by inventory)
- Out: Visibility scoring — see e09-visibility-model
- Out: Noise propagation — see e09-sound-propagation
## Notes
Default multipliers: stand-sprint noise 1.0, stand-run 0.6, stand-walk 0.3, crouch-walk 0.15, slow-walk 0.08, still 0.0. Related: e09 consumes; do not implement scoring here.

**Integration note:** Promoted to P0/m1 — visibility and noise at m1 need crouch/walk/run profiles.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a crouched player moving at crouch speed, when the profile is read, then noise multiplier is 0.15 and silhouette height matches the crouch capsule.
- AC-2 [unit] Given sprint pressed while crouched, when resolved, then the player stands (if space allows) and profile becomes stand-sprint; if a ceiling blocks standing, sprint is ignored (edge).
- AC-3 [unit] Given an encumbrance multiplier 1.5 from armor, when walking, then noise multiplier is 0.45 and clamped to ≤ 1.0 overall.
- AC-4 [content] Given the stance profile table, when validated, then every stance × gait combination is defined.

items.title: Emit footstep events tagged with surface material and gait
items.description:
## Why
Surfaces matter to stealth (Thief constitution) and footsteps are a key audio feedback channel (E28).
## What
As a thief, I want gravel to be louder than carpet and wet stone to sound different so that I choose my path deliberately.

The sim emits footstep events at stride intervals carrying position, foot, surface material (from world properties of the ground collider), wetness/frozen state, gait and loudness = profile noise × material loudness.
## Scope
- In: Stride-distance based footstep cadence per gait
- In: Ground material lookup via e03-world-properties (including wet, frozen, burning states)
- In: Event consumed by audio and stealth (via event bus)
- Out: Sound propagation/perception — see e09-sound-propagation
- Out: Footstep SFX assets — see mw-e38
## Notes
Material loudness examples (data): carpet 0.3, wood 0.7, stone 0.8, gravel 1.2, shallow water 1.3, ice 0.9. Loudness is data, not code.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a player walking 10 m at walk speed, when footsteps are counted, then the count equals floor(10 / strideLength) ± 1.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the ground collider has material gravel, when a step lands, then event.material = gravel and loudness = profileNoise × 1.2.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a stone floor with wet=0.8, when stepping, then the event carries wet=true and loudness uses the wet-stone modifier.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the player is airborne or standing still, when ticks elapse, then no footstep events are emitted (edge).

items.title: Mantle onto and grab ledges detected from world geometry
items.description:
## Why
Classes change possibilities: "the thief might climb through a window". Verticality is also a stealth factor. Every class needs baseline mantling; thieves go further.
## What
As a player, I want to jump at a ledge and pull myself up so that I can reach windows, crates and balconies.

Ledge detection uses forward + down shape casts against surfaces with the ledge/climbable markup, validates headroom and standing space, and performs: auto-mantle (≤ 1.0 m), mantle (≤ 1.6 m, all classes), ledge grab/hang with shimmy and pull-up (≤ 2.2 m reach, capability-gated), and drop-down to hang from an edge.
## Scope
- In: Ledge query + validation (headroom, surface angle ≤ 20°, clearance)
- In: Mantle, ledge hang, shimmy, pull-up, drop, jump-back states
- In: Capability gates (e.g. ledge hang may require climbing capability per class data)
- Out: Free climbing walls — see e02-climb-surfaces
- Out: Surface markup authoring — see e03-climbable-surfaces
## Notes
Mantle is deterministic and uses sim-driven motion curves, not root motion. Heavy encumbrance may block pull-up (data).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a 1.4 m crate edge ahead and jump pressed while moving forward, when resolved, then the player mantles onto the top in 0.6 s ± 0.05 and ends grounded on it.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a ledge with 1.0 m headroom above it, when mantle is attempted, then it is rejected unless crouched mantle fits (capsule check) (edge).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a player hanging from a ledge, when moving sideways, then they shimmy at 1.0 m/s and stop at ledge ends or gaps > 0.3 m.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a class without ledge-hang capability, when jumping at a 2.0 m ledge, then no grab occurs and the player falls normally.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a ledge surface that becomes frozen or burning (via e03 properties), when hanging, then the player is forced to drop after the configured grace time (1.0 s).
- AC-6 [integration] Given the greybox traversal course, when the golden mantle replay runs, then state hashes match.

items.title: Climb ladders, ivy, ropes and rough walls marked climbable
items.description:
## Why
Climbing is a core thief verb and an alternate-route generator; burning the ivy or freezing the wall should change it (systemic).
## What
As a thief, I want to climb any surface the world marks as climbable so that I can find routes others cannot.

Climb state attaches the player to a climbable surface (ladder, rope, ivy, rough stone), moves in surface space, transitions to ledge mantle at the top, and detaches on jump-off. Climbability comes only from world properties (climbable grade + capability requirement), so fire removing ivy or ice making walls slippery works automatically.
## Scope
- In: Climb attach/detach, surface-space movement (0.8 m/s default), corner transitions ≤ 45°
- In: Ropes (vertical, swaying anchor) and ladders (all classes), grade-gated walls (thief capability)
- In: Stamina hook (value from progression) and fall on stamina exhaustion
- Out: Climbing claws/tools — see mw-e10
- Out: Rope arrows — see mw-e05 (they spawn a climbable rope entity)
## Notes
Rope arrows, vines spell, and a knight propping a ladder all work by spawning entities with the climbable property — no special cases.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a surface with climbable=ladder, when any class presses toward it, then they attach and climb at 1.2 m/s.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a surface with climbable=rough and requiresCapability=climb.rough, when a class without it approaches, then no attach occurs; with it, attach succeeds.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a climbing player whose ivy surface loses the climbable property (e.g. burned away), when the next tick runs, then the player detaches and falls (edge).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a runtime-spawned rope entity with climbable=rope, when approached, then the player can climb it exactly like an authored rope.
- AC-5 [unit] Given stamina reaches 0 while climbing, when the tick runs, then the player slips and falls.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the greybox climbing wall, when the bot climbs to the top and mantles, then it reaches the upper platform with no console errors.

items.title: Wade and swim in water and slide on frozen surfaces
items.description:
## Why
"Magic can freeze water … open traversal opportunities." Freezing a lake to walk across it must emerge from properties, not a scripted bridge.
## What
As a sorcerer, I want to freeze a river and walk across it so that magic opens new routes.

Water volumes (from e03) drive wading (depth 0.5–1.2 m, speed reduction), swimming (> 1.2 m; no weapons, limited breath), and diving. Frozen water becomes a walkable solid with low friction (ice sliding, reduced accel). Melting ice drops the player back into water.
## Scope
- In: Wade/swim/dive states, breath meter (20 s default), drowning damage hook
- In: Low-friction movement on any surface with frozen state or friction < 0.2
- In: Transitions when water freezes/melts under the player
- Out: Water/freezing simulation — see e03-water-wetness, e03-freeze-melt
- Out: Drowning damage numbers — see e04-damage-model
## Notes
Swimming makes the player wet (sets wet property on the actor), which matters for fire and electricity.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given water depth 0.9 m, when moving, then the player wades at 60% run speed and footstep events report material water.
- AC-2 [unit] Given depth 1.5 m, when entered, then the player swims, breath depletes over 20 s underwater, and damage events fire each 1 s after depletion.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a water volume transitions to frozen while the player swims on the surface, when resolved, then the player is placed on top of the ice rather than embedded in it (edge).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a frozen surface, when the player stops input at run speed, then they slide ≥ 2.0 m before stopping (vs ≤ 0.5 m on stone).
- AC-5 [unit] Given the player stands on ice that melts, when the tick runs, then the player drops into the water volume and state becomes wading/swimming.
- AC-6 [unit] Given the player exits a water volume, when checked, then the actor wet property is set to 1.0 and decays per e03 drying rules.

items.title: Apply knockback, launches and fall damage to the player controller
items.description:
## Why
Gust, Thunderclap, explosions, trolls and collapsing floors must move the player through one impulse API; failure (being blasted off a ledge) creates stories.
## What
As a player, I want explosions and heavy blows to physically throw me so that the world feels powerful and dangerous.

The controller accepts impulses from any source (force stimulus from e03, attacks from e04), transitions to a ragdoll-free "launched" airborne state with reduced air control, and computes fall damage from impact speed via data thresholds. Self-cast impulses (a sorcerer using Gust on themselves) are allowed — "too useful" is permitted.
## Scope
- In: Impulse API (vector, source, stagger flag), launched state, recovery
- In: Fall damage curve (safe ≤ 8 m/s impact, lethal ≥ 20 m/s) as data
- In: Landing into water or soft materials (hay, snow) reduces damage via material property
- Out: Stagger/poise — see e04-damage-model
## Notes
Soft landing uses a material property (impactAbsorb) so hay carts and snowdrifts work automatically.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an impulse of 10 m/s horizontal + 5 m/s up, when applied to a grounded player, then the player enters launched state and follows the ballistic arc within 1% error.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an impact speed of 7 m/s, when landing, then no damage event fires; at 14 m/s a damage event matching the data curve fires.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a landing surface with impactAbsorb=0.8 (hay), when landing at 14 m/s, then damage is reduced by 80%.
- AC-4 [unit] Given two impulses in the same tick, when resolved, then they sum and the result is order-independent (deterministic).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a launched player hits a wall mid-flight, when resolved, then horizontal velocity is removed and wall-impact damage uses the same curve (edge).

items.title: Lock on to and cycle between targets with camera framing
items.description:
## Why
Knight and archer combat need reliable targeting; poor lock-on makes intrinsically fun combat frustrating.
## What
As a knight, I want to lock onto an enemy and circle-strafe around it so that I can focus on timing and positioning.

Target selection in sim (targetable component, distance ≤ 20 m, within 60° of camera forward, LOS), cycling left/right by screen angle, strafing movement relative to target, lock break on distance > 25 m or LOS lost for > 1.0 s, and camera framing of player + target.
## Scope
- In: Targetable component with lock point(s) and priority
- In: Selection, cycle, break rules; strafe mode in controller
- In: Camera framing lerp that keeps both in view
- Out: Weak-point targeting on bows — see e05-bow-core
- Out: Soft aim assist for spells — see e06-spell-pipeline
## Notes
Targetables can be creatures, but also shootable mechanisms and interactables flagged lockable (lets archers lock onto a distant bell).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given three targetables within the cone, when lock is pressed, then the one nearest the camera forward axis (weighted by distance) is selected, deterministically.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a lock on target A, when cycle-right is pressed, then the next target clockwise in screen angle is selected; with no other targets, lock stays on A.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a locked target moves behind a wall, when 1.0 s elapses without LOS, then the lock breaks; if LOS returns at 0.8 s, the lock persists (edge).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a locked target dies, when resolved, then the lock auto-switches to the next valid target within 10 m or releases.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a lock-on, when move=(1,0), then the player strafes around the target maintaining distance within 5% per second.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the greybox arena with 3 dummies, when the bot locks and cycles, then the HUD lock marker moves across all three and no console errors occur.

items.title: Pick up, carry, drop and throw liftable objects
items.description:
## Why
Throwing a bottle to distract a guard, stacking crates to reach a window, or carrying a body out of sight are core systemic verbs.
## What
As a thief, I want to pick up a bottle and throw it so that the noise draws the guard away.

Any entity with liftable and weight ≤ the actor carry limit can be picked up via interaction, held in front (collides), dropped, placed precisely, or thrown with a charge (0.2–1.0 s → 4–14 m/s). Thrown objects are physics objects: they deal impact via e03, break if fragile, and emit noise events. Bodies (unconscious/dead actors) are carriable with slow movement.
## Scope
- In: Carry limit per class (data), carry pose, drop/place/throw
- In: Throw arc preview line (UI hint)
- In: Carrying bodies (heavy carry: 50% speed, no jump)
- Out: Telekinesis lifting — see e03-liftable-levitation (magic uses the same object side)
- Out: Distraction AI response — see mw-e11
## Notes
A thrown burning object remains burning; a thrown oil flask shatters and spills oil (fragile + contents). No special cases — all via properties.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a liftable object weighing 8 kg and a carry limit of 25 kg, when Interact is used, then the object is held; given 40 kg, then the affordance is unavailable with reason "Too heavy".
- AC-2 [unit] Given a held object and throw charged for 1.0 s, when released, then it leaves at 14 m/s ± 0.1 along the aim direction.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a thrown fragile object, when it impacts above its break threshold, then it breaks via e03-breakables and a noise event with the break loudness is emitted.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a held object is set on fire (burning property), when still held after 2.0 s, then the actor takes heat exposure and auto-drops it (edge).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a held object would clip into a wall, when carried, then it is pushed back and never penetrates geometry by > 2 cm.
- AC-6 [unit] Given the player carries a body, when moving, then speed is 50% and jump is disabled.

items.title: Push and pull heavy objects such as crates and statues
items.description:
## Why
Manipulating statues and moving objects are explicit puzzle examples (Puzzle constitution); knights should shove what others can only drag.
## What
As a player, I want to grab a heavy crate and push or pull it so that I can reach high ledges or weigh down pressure plates.

Objects with pushable=true enter a grab state; movement speed scales with weight vs. actor strength (data), restricted to the object axes if the object declares them (grid statues, rails). Pushing across frozen surfaces is easier (friction from properties).
## Scope
- In: Grab/release, push/pull speed curve by weight and surface friction
- In: Axis/rail-constrained pushables and grid-snapped pushables (for puzzles)
- In: Rotate-in-place affordance for rotatable statues/mirrors
- Out: Puzzle-specific prefabs — see e15-prefab-pieces
## Notes
Speed = base × clamp(strength / (weight × friction), 0, 1); knight strength higher. Friction from world properties (ice ~0.05).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a 120 kg crate on stone and a strength profile of 150, when pushed, then movement speed equals the documented formula within 1%.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same crate on a frozen surface, when pushed, then speed is higher than on stone and the crate continues sliding 1.0 m ± 0.2 after release.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a grid-snapped statue, when a push is released mid-cell, then it completes to the next cell centre.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a pushable blocked by a wall or another object, when pushed, then neither the player nor the object moves and no penetration occurs (edge).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a rotatable mirror, when rotate is used, then it turns by its configured step (15°) and emits a rotation-changed event.

items.title: Run a controller feel review and retune against reference games
items.description:
## Why
Automated tests keep the controller correct; only humans can tell if it feels excellent. Numeric targets need validating against the tone references (Souls weight, Zelda responsiveness).
## What
Time-boxed (1 day) playtest of the greybox traversal course with 3+ testers, comparing jump arc, acceleration, camera lag and mantle timing against reference feel notes. Output: tuning changes committed to controller data and a short findings doc.
## Scope
- In: Playtest script, questionnaire, tuning deltas
- In: docs/design/controller-feel.md with before/after values
- Out: Combat feel — see mw-e04
## Notes
Time-box: 1 day. Record sessions (e34 telemetry optional).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given 3 testers on the traversal course, when surveyed, then median "controls feel responsive" score is ≥ 4/5.
- AC-2 [content] Given the review, when finished, then all tuning changes are committed to controller data and golden replays are re-blessed with diffs attached.
- AC-3 [manual] Given any tester reports a specific frustration (e.g. missed mantle), when reviewed, then it is either fixed or filed as a bead with a failing test.

items.title: Define typed world-property components for systemic interactions
items.description:
## Why
The single most important architectural principle: interactions come from properties (flammable=true), never "Fireball + Rope" scripts. Every system in the game reads and writes these.
## What
As a designer, I want to give any object a set of physical/elemental properties so that it automatically reacts to fire, water, cold, electricity, force and light.

A typed property component set in src/sim with schema in src/content: material, temperature (°C), ignitionPoint, fuel (burn seconds), burning, wetness (0..1), frozen, freezePoint, conductive, charge, weight (kg), fragile (breakThreshold J), hp/structural, buoyancy/density, climbable (grade), liftable, pushable, hideable, reflective, transparent, opaque, lightEmitter, soundDamping, friction, impactAbsorb, ownership tag. Derived queries (isFlammableNow = flammable ∧ ¬wet>0.5 ∧ ¬frozen).
## Scope
- In: Property component definitions + zod schemas + defaults
- In: Query helpers and change events (propertyChanged{entity, key, old, new})
- In: Deterministic ordered iteration over entities with a property
- Out: Material defaults — see e03-material-presets
- Out: Propagation behaviour — see e03-element-propagation and siblings
## Notes
Keep the property set closed and versioned (adding a property is a schema bump tracked by e30 migrations). A CI guard (see epic exit criteria) forbids type-pair checks in interaction rules. Actors (player, creatures) use the same components — see e03-actor-properties.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an entity with flammable, wetness=0.8, when isFlammableNow is queried, then it returns false; at wetness=0.2 it returns true.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a property write that changes a value, when committed, then exactly one propertyChanged event fires with old/new values; writing the same value fires none.
- AC-3 [content] Given an entity data file with an unknown property key or out-of-range value (wetness 1.4), when validated, then validation fails naming the path.
- AC-4 [unit] Given 1,000 entities with the flammable property created in random order, when iterated, then iteration order is by entity id and stable across runs.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a frozen=true entity with temperature above freezePoint, when invariants are checked, then the validator reports an inconsistent state (edge).

items.title: Provide data-defined material presets for common world objects
items.description:
## Why
Fast content creation: a designer should mark a crate "wood" and get sensible flammability, weight density, sound and fragility for free.
## What
As a designer, I want to pick a material preset (wood, dry-wood, stone, iron, copper, cloth, rope, paper, oil, water, ice, glass, straw/hay, flesh, bone, ivy, earth) so that objects get consistent properties with per-object overrides.
## Scope
- In: content/materials/*.json presets with property defaults + footstep loudness + impact sound id
- In: Override merge rules (object value > preset > global default)
- In: Material docs table generated from data
- Out: Visual materials/shaders — see mw-e37 / mw-e29
## Notes
Example values: wood ignition 300°C, fuel 60 s/kg-ish scalar; iron conductive, non-flammable; oil ignition 210°C, spreads as liquid; glass fragile threshold low; straw impactAbsorb 0.8, very flammable.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given every material preset, when validated, then all fields pass schema and physically inconsistent combos (flammable + ignitionPoint missing) are rejected.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an object with material=wood and override weight=3, when resolved, then weight is 3 and all other properties come from the wood preset.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an object referencing an unknown material id, when loaded, then load fails with the id and file path (edge).
- AC-4 [content] Given the presets, when the docs generator runs, then docs/design/materials.md lists every material and property value.

items.title: Inject heat, cold, water, charge, force and gas via one stimulus API
items.description:
## Why
Spells, arrows, torches, lightning, creatures and traps must all act on the world through the same door, or the combinatorial workload kills the project.
## What
As a developer, I want a single applyStimulus(shape, element, intensity, duration, source) API so that any ability produces world effects without knowing what it hits.

Stimulus shapes: point, sphere, cone, capsule/beam, box, contact (on hit). Elements: heat, cold, water, charge, force (impulse), gas (type), light, blunt/slash/pierce (for breakables). Each stimulus is recorded with source for attribution (quests, crime, telemetry). Stimuli resolve in a fixed phase of the tick.
## Scope
- In: Stimulus types + shapes, ordering rules, attribution
- In: Overlap resolution against entities with properties and against the element field
- In: Stimulus log available to debug overlay and tests
- Out: Specific spells/arrows — see e06-spell-pipeline, e05-bow-core
- Out: Propagation after injection — see e03-element-propagation
## Notes
A Fire Arrow = contact(pierce) + sphere(heat, r=0.5). A torch swing = capsule(heat, low). Thunderclap = sphere(force) + sphere(blunt). Designers compose these in data.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a sphere heat stimulus of radius 2 m, when applied, then every entity with temperature within 2 m receives heat scaled by the documented falloff and entities outside receive none.
- AC-2 [unit] Given two stimuli applied in the same tick in either order, when resolved, then resulting state is identical (order-independent via sorted resolution).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a force stimulus on a pushable 10 kg object, when applied, then an impulse proportional to intensity/weight is delivered to the physics object.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a stimulus with a source entity, when it causes a propertyChanged, then the event carries the source id (attribution).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a stimulus with intensity 0 or a zero-radius shape, when applied, then it is a no-op and does not throw (edge).

items.title: Build a sparse spatial grid for temperature, moisture, gas and charge
items.description:
## Why
Fire spreading across a floor, gas filling a room, or water pooling need a medium between objects; per-object rules alone cannot express "the room is full of gas".
## What
A sparse, chunked voxel field (default 0.5 m cells, 8×8×8 chunks) storing temperature, moisture, gas concentration per gas type, and charge. Supports diffusion steps with per-cell conductivity derived from occupying materials, walls blocking flow, sleeping chunks when stable, and entity↔cell exchange.
## Scope
- In: Chunked sparse storage, activation/sleep, fixed-point or deterministic float math
- In: Diffusion kernel with blockers from static geometry
- In: Entity↔cell coupling interface used by propagation rules
- Out: Element-specific rules — see e03-element-propagation, e03-water-wetness, e03-gas-clouds, e03-electricity
## Notes
Use integer/fixed-point for cross-browser determinism. Budget target: 2,000 active cells ≤ 2.0 ms/tick (verified by e03-sim-perf-budget).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a single hot cell in an open field, when diffusion runs for N ticks, then total heat is conserved within 0.1% (minus configured ambient loss).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a wall between two cells, when diffusion runs, then no quantity crosses the wall.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a chunk whose values are within epsilon of ambient for 60 ticks, when checked, then it sleeps and costs zero update time until touched.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the same initial field on two runs, when stepped 1,000 ticks, then field hashes are identical.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a stimulus far outside any existing chunk (1 km away), when applied, then a new chunk is allocated without affecting others and memory stays bounded by the chunk cap (edge).

items.title: Ignite, burn, spread and extinguish fire from heat and properties
items.description:
## Why
Fire is the canonical systemic element: burning ropes, oil slicks, torched webs, scared creatures. "If ropes have flammable=true and fire spells produce heat, you have built the foundation."
## What
As a player, I want anything flammable to catch fire when hot enough and fire to spread to nearby flammables so that I can improvise with torches and spells.

Heat/fire rules over properties and the element field: entities heat up from stimuli and neighbouring cells; at ignitionPoint and not wet/frozen they ignite; burning entities consume fuel, emit heat into the field, emit light (via e03-light-field) and smoke gas, dry out neighbours, and reduce structural hp; at fuel 0 they become burnt (material → charred) or are destroyed. Water/cold/smothering extinguish. This item also establishes the propagation rule framework (rule registry, phases) that other elements plug into.
## Scope
- In: Rule framework: ordered rule phases, each rule reads/writes only properties + field
- In: Heating, ignition, burning, fuel consumption, burnout/destruction, spread via field
- In: Extinguish by wetness/cold/smother; wet objects dry by heat before igniting
- Out: Water, ice, electricity, gas specifics — see sibling e03 items
- Out: Fire visuals/audio — see e03-state-feedback-bridge
## Notes
Everything here is expressed as property rules. A lint rule forbids referencing entity archetype ids in src/sim/elements/**. Emergent examples to cover in e03-emergence-scenarios: oil puddle ignition chain, burning a rope support, torching a spider web wall.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given any entity with flammable, wetness < 0.5 and not frozen, when its temperature reaches ignitionPoint, then burning=true on that tick.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a burning entity and a flammable neighbour within 1 cell, when ticks elapse, then the neighbour ignites within the time predicted by field heat transfer (± 1 tick) and a non-flammable neighbour never ignites.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a burning entity with fuel F, when it burns uninterrupted, then it burns out after F seconds and transitions to its burnt state (material charred or destroyed per data).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a wet flammable entity (wetness 1.0) exposed to heat, when heated, then wetness decreases first and it ignites only after wetness < 0.5.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a burning entity receives a water stimulus making wetness ≥ 0.5, when resolved, then burning=false and a steam gas puff is emitted into the field.
- AC-6 [unit] Given a fire in a closed room with limited fuel, when simulated 10 minutes, then the fire terminates (no infinite burn loop) and the field returns to ambient (edge).
- AC-7 [integration] Given a greybox scene with a line of 10 wooden crates, when the first is ignited, then all 10 burn in order and a replay reproduces identical state hashes.

items.title: Simulate water volumes, splashes, wetness and drying
items.description:
## Why
Water extinguishes fire, conducts electricity, freezes into bridges and makes creatures vulnerable — it is the most combinatorial element after fire.
## What
As a player, I want water to soak things and put out flames so that dousing a torch or soaking a goblin before a lightning spell just works.

Water volumes (lakes, basins, puddles) with level and drain/fill rates; water stimuli (splash, rain, spell) raise entity wetness and cell moisture; wetness decays by heat and time; entities submerged in a volume become fully wet; puddles spawn from spilled liquid; liquid types (water, oil) share the volume model with different properties (oil floats, flammable).
## Scope
- In: Water volume entity (level, fill/drain), submersion checks, puddle spawning from spills
- In: Wetness gain/decay rules; rain zone stimulus
- In: Liquid types: water, oil (flammable, slippery)
- Out: Freezing — see e03-freeze-melt
- Out: Fluid dynamics / flowing rivers simulation — out of scope (volumes are level-based)
## Notes
Basins with drains/valves are puzzle pieces (see e15-prefab-pieces). Oil on water floats and can burn on the surface — emergent, not scripted.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given any entity fully inside a water volume, when a tick runs, then its wetness becomes 1.0.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a wet entity (1.0) at 20°C ambient and no heat source, when time passes, then wetness decays to ≤ 0.1 within the documented drying time; near a burning entity it dries at least 3× faster.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a basin with a drain opened, when ticks run, then level decreases at the drain rate and entities previously submerged emerge when level falls below them.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an oil liquid spilled onto a water volume, when resolved, then an oil layer sits on the surface and igniting it burns the surface layer only.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a water stimulus onto a non-absorbent material (iron), when resolved, then wetness rises but caps at the material absorbency max (edge).

items.title: Freeze water and wet objects into ice and melt them with heat
items.description:
## Why
"Magic can freeze water." Frozen rivers as bridges, frozen doors that shatter, ice surfaces for sliding enemies are signature "Wait… I can do that?" moments.
## What
As a sorcerer, I want cold to freeze water and wet things so that I can make bridges, jam mechanisms and shatter frozen objects.

Cold stimuli lower temperature; water volume cells and wet entities below freezePoint become frozen: water volume surface becomes a walkable ice solid (thickness grows with exposure), wet entities gain frozen (immobilised mechanisms, brittle → fragile multiplier), creatures slowed/frozen via actor properties. Heat melts; ice slabs are physics objects that float and can be broken.
## Scope
- In: Freezing/melting rules with latent time, ice thickness per cell
- In: Frozen water surface colliders generated/removed deterministically
- In: Frozen modifiers: mechanisms jam, fragility ×3, friction → ice
- Out: Player sliding/walking on ice — see e02-water-ice-traversal
- Out: Frost spells — see mw-e08
## Notes
Jammed mechanisms: any mechanism entity with frozen=true refuses to move (e.g. freeze a portcullis winch to stop it closing). Ice collider changes must notify physics to wake bodies resting on it.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a water volume cell at the surface receiving cold until temperature ≤ freezePoint, when resolved, then an ice collider with thickness ≥ 0.1 m exists at that cell and thickness grows with continued cold up to 0.5 m.
- AC-2 [unit] Given any wet entity (wetness ≥ 0.3) cooled below freezePoint, when resolved, then frozen=true and its fragility threshold is divided by 3.
- AC-3 [unit] Given any mechanism entity with frozen=true, when a signal tries to move it, then it does not move and emits a jammed event until thawed.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an ice surface with an object resting on it, when heat melts it, then the collider is removed and the object falls/floats into the water volume on the same tick.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a dry entity (wetness 0) cooled far below freezing, when resolved, then it becomes cold but not frozen (edge: freezing requires water).
- AC-6 [integration] Given the greybox river, when a cold stimulus is swept across it, then the bot can walk across the resulting ice and a replay reproduces the same hashes.

items.title: Conduct electrical charge through conductive and wet objects
items.description:
## Why
Storm magic becomes spectacular when lightning arcs through a puddle into three goblins standing in it, or powers an old mechanism — pure property combos.
## What
As a sorcerer, I want lightning to spread through water and metal so that I can electrify puddles, armored knights or arcane conduits.

Charge stimuli add charge to entities/cells; charge flows along connected conductive networks (conductive property or wetness ≥ 0.5, or water volumes) with per-hop falloff within one tick; charge above thresholds deals shock (actors), ignites flammables at high intensity, and powers "charge receiver" mechanisms (arcane conduits, old dwarven lifts).
## Scope
- In: Connectivity graph build from contacts/overlaps, cached and invalidated on movement/wetness change
- In: Charge distribution with falloff, discharge, shock event, ignition at threshold
- In: Charge receiver component feeding the signal system
- Out: Storm spells — see mw-e08
- Out: Damage numbers — see e04-damage-model
## Notes
Network flood fill capped (e.g. 256 nodes) with deterministic BFS by entity id. A knight in metal armor is conductive via actor properties (e03-actor-properties).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a water volume containing three actors, when a charge stimulus hits the water, then all three receive a shock event with intensity reduced by the documented falloff per hop.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a chain of conductive entities touching, when charge enters one end, then charge reaches the far end in the same tick; with a non-conductive gap, it does not cross.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a dry wooden entity next to a charged metal entity, when resolved, then the wood receives no charge; once wetness ≥ 0.5 it conducts.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a charge receiver in a charged network, when charge ≥ its activation threshold, then it emits an activated signal; below threshold it does not.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a conductive network larger than the node cap, when charge floods, then propagation stops at the cap deterministically and logs a warning (edge).

items.title: Spread gas, smoke and steam clouds that react to fire and wind
items.description:
## Why
Gust clearing poisonous gas, igniting swamp gas, smoke blocking sight lines for a thief escape — gas turns rooms into systemic spaces.
## What
As a thief, I want smoke to block vision and flammable gas to explode when lit so that I can escape or set traps.

Gas types in the element field (smoke: blocks vision; steam: obscures, scalds lightly; poison: damages actors; flammable/marsh gas: ignites with flash + force stimulus when concentration ≥ threshold). Gas diffuses, rises/sinks by type, is blocked by walls/doors, vents through openings, and is pushed by force stimuli (Gust).
## Scope
- In: Gas species data (buoyancy, diffusion, decay, effects)
- In: Ignition of flammable gas → explosion stimulus
- In: Visibility occlusion query for stealth/AI (density along a ray)
- Out: AI reaction to smoke — see mw-e11
- Out: Gas VFX — see e29-vfx-framework
## Notes
Closed doors block gas (door entities are field blockers) — opening a door lets smoke pour out.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given flammable gas at concentration ≥ threshold in a cell and a heat source ≥ ignition, when resolved, then the gas is consumed and a force + heat stimulus is applied with radius scaled by the consumed volume.
- AC-2 [unit] Given smoke between an observer and a target, when densityAlongRay is queried, then it returns the integrated density and exceeds the vision-block threshold for a 2 m thick cloud.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a closed door separating two rooms, when gas fills room A, then room B stays at 0 until the door opens, after which concentration equalises over time.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a force stimulus through a gas cloud, when applied, then gas is displaced along the force direction by the documented amount.
- AC-5 [unit] Given gas in a fully sealed room with no decay source, when simulated for 30 minutes, then total gas mass is conserved and no cell exceeds max concentration (edge).

items.title: Simulate movable, throwable and stackable physics objects in sim
items.description:
## Why
Crates, barrels, bottles, statues and debris are the raw material of systemic play and puzzles; they must behave consistently and deterministically.
## What
As a player, I want objects to tumble, stack and roll believably so that I can build, knock over and improvise.

A physics-object layer binding e03 properties (weight → mass, friction, restitution, buoyancy) to rigid bodies stepped inside the sim fixed timestep, with sleeping, impact events (impulse, relative speed, materials), and sim-side authority (renderer interpolates only). Impact events feed breakables, noise and damage.
## Scope
- In: Rigid body lifecycle from properties; fixed-step integration inside sim tick
- In: Impact events with energy (J) and material pair for sound/noise
- In: Stacking stability, sleeping, max-body budget, render interpolation contract
- Out: Breaking — see e03-breakables
- Out: Player carry/push — see e02-carry-throw, e02-push-pull
- Out: Levitation — see e03-liftable-levitation
## Notes
Physics engine per e00-engine-decision (Rapier WASM with enhanced determinism expected). Physics is wrapped behind an interface so unit tests can run with a deterministic reference integrator.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a 10 kg crate dropped from 2 m onto stone, when simulated, then it comes to rest within 2 s and emits one impact event with energy 196 J ± 5%.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a stack of 5 crates, when simulated for 10 s with no disturbance, then no crate moves more than 1 cm (stable stacking) and all bodies sleep.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a weight property change on a body (e.g. soaked cloth heavier), when committed, then the rigid body mass updates on the next tick.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the same scene and inputs, when simulated 3,000 ticks on two runs, then physics state hashes are identical.
- AC-5 [unit] Given the active body count exceeds the budget (default 300), when a new body wakes, then the oldest distant resting bodies are forced to sleep and a budget warning is logged (edge).
- AC-6 [perf] Given 200 active bodies in the greybox scene, when simulated, then physics step ≤ 2.0 ms per tick p95 on the reference machine.

items.title: Break fragile objects and smash weakened walls into debris
items.description:
## Why
"The knight might discover that an old wall can simply be smashed apart." Breaking must come from damage type vs. structural properties, so arrows, spells and thrown barrels break things too.
## What
As a knight, I want to smash cracked walls, barricades and pottery so that brute force opens new routes and reveals secrets.

Breakable component: structural hp, resistances per damage type (blunt, slash, pierce, force, fire, cold-shatter), fragile impact threshold, break result (debris pieces, contents spilled, nav/collision change, revealed passage). Weak walls are visually telegraphed (crack decal hook) and marked with a discoverable hint property.
## Scope
- In: Damage accumulation per type, impact-energy breaks for fragile objects, frozen-shatter multiplier
- In: Break results: spawn debris bodies (budgeted), drop contents, remove collider, update nav hooks
- In: Break events with source attribution and noise loudness
- Out: Weapon damage numbers — see e04-damage-model
- Out: Persisting broken state — see e27-entity-deltas
## Notes
Barricades of wood: slash-weak and flammable (burn through them). Old walls: blunt/force-weak only — so knight, Thunderclap, a rolling boulder or an explosive gas pocket all work. No per-class checks.

**Integration note:** Promoted to P0/m1 — e27-entity-deltas persists broken state; a breakable crate is part of the grey-box slice.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a breakable with blunt resistance 0.2 and hp 100, when it receives blunt damage totalling 125, then it breaks; the same slash damage with resistance 0.9 does not break it.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a fragile object, when an impact event exceeds its break threshold (from any source: thrown, fallen, hit), then it breaks and spills its contents.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a frozen breakable, when struck, then its effective threshold is divided by the frozen fragility multiplier.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a break, when resolved, then the collider is removed, a revealed-passage event fires if configured, and a noise event with the material break loudness is emitted.
- AC-5 [unit] Given many breaks in one tick exceeding the debris budget, when resolved, then extra debris is culled deterministically (oldest first) and breaks still complete (edge).
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the greybox weak-wall room, when the bot uses a heavy attack placeholder on the wall, then a passage opens and the bot walks through.

items.title: Let external forces hold, levitate and fling liftable objects
items.description:
## Why
Mage Hand, Telekinesis, Gravity Well and "throwing creatures / catching projectiles" all need one world-side API for being held and moved at a distance.
## What
As a sorcerer, I want to lift a crate onto a balcony, pull a lever from across a chasm or yank a shield from a goblin so that magic manipulates the world itself.

A holdable-at-distance API: external holders attach a spring-damper constraint to any body with liftable=true (or actors with a liftable tier), limited by holder strength vs. weight, with gravity scale overrides (float), point attractors (Gravity Well), and release with velocity. Interactables (levers) can be actuated remotely if flagged remoteActuatable.
## Scope
- In: Remote hold constraint, strength vs weight check, break-hold on obstruction or overload
- In: Gravity scale override zones and point attractors
- In: Remote actuation of interactables with remoteActuatable
- Out: The spells themselves — see e06-spell-pipeline / mw-e08
- Out: Player hand-carry — see e02-carry-throw
## Notes
Standing on a levitated platform should work (it is just a moving body; controller handles moving-platform carry). Catching projectiles: arrows are liftable light bodies.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a liftable 30 kg object and a holder strength of 50, when held, then it tracks the target point with settling time ≤ 0.5 s; given 80 kg, the hold fails with reason overweight.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a held object blocked by a wall for > 1.0 s with the target far behind it, when resolved, then the hold breaks and the object drops (edge).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a point attractor of strength S, when loose liftable objects are within radius, then each accelerates toward the point proportional to S/mass and non-liftable objects are unaffected.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a remoteActuatable lever within the holder range, when remote actuation is applied, then the lever toggles exactly as if interacted with; a lever without the flag does not.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a held object released with velocity v, when released, then its initial velocity equals v within 1%.

items.title: Support hanging objects on ropes that burn, cut or snap
items.description:
## Why
Shooting the rope that holds a chandelier onto enemies, burning a rope bridge behind you, or cutting a hanging cage free are classic emergent moments.
## What
As an archer, I want to shoot or burn a rope so that whatever it holds falls — chandeliers, cages, drawbridges, counterweights, bridges.

Rope/chain support entities connect an anchor to a supported body; they have material properties (rope: flammable, slash/pierce-weak; chain: not). When hp reaches 0 or burnt, the support releases, the supported object becomes dynamic (falling damage via impact) and any linked mechanism receives a signal. Rope bridges are chains of planks supported by ropes.
## Scope
- In: Support constraint entity with hp/resistances and load
- In: Release → dynamic body + signal output
- In: Rope bridge prefab (planks + two support ropes)
- Out: Climbable ropes — see e02-climb-surfaces (a rope can be both climbable and a support)
## Notes
Overload: a support snaps if load weight exceeds its rating — putting a heavy crate on a rotten rope bridge snaps it (failure creates stories).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given any support with flammable material, when it burns out, then it releases and the supported body becomes dynamic on that tick.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a rope support with pierce resistance 0.3, when hit by pierce damage ≥ its hp/0.7, then it releases; a chain support with pierce immunity does not.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a released support linked to a mechanism, when released, then the mechanism receives a signal exactly once.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a rope bridge rated for 150 kg, when total load exceeds 150 kg, then the weakest rope snaps and planks fall (edge/failure).
- AC-5 [integration] Given the greybox chandelier room, when a pierce stimulus hits the rope, then the chandelier falls and impact damage events fire for actors beneath it.

items.title: Float and sink objects in liquid volumes by density
items.description:
## Why
Floating crates as stepping stones, sinking a heavy chest to trip a submerged plate, or ice slabs drifting are cheap emergent traversal once density is a property.
## What
As a player, I want wooden objects to float and iron to sink so that I can improvise rafts and stepping stones.

Buoyancy force from submerged volume × liquid density vs. object density, with drag; objects adjust to the liquid level; wet/soaked materials may change density (data).
## Scope
- In: Buoyancy + drag forces for bodies in liquid volumes
- In: Standing on floating bodies (moving platform)
- In: Density changes from waterlogging (data)
- Out: Currents / flowing rivers — out of scope for MVP
## Notes
Ice (density 0.92) floats automatically once frozen slabs break free.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an object with density 0.6 in water (1.0), when settled, then 60% ± 5% of its volume is submerged.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an iron object (density 7.8), when placed in water, then it sinks to the bottom and can rest on a submerged pressure plate.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a floating crate with a 20 kg load exceeding its buoyancy reserve, when loaded, then it sinks (edge).
- AC-4 [unit] Given the water level drops (drain), when resolved, then floating objects descend with the surface and settle on the floor.

items.title: Query light level at any position from all light sources in sim
items.description:
## Why
Stealth needs light and darkness as numbers; puzzles need "navigating darkness" and light receivers. The renderer's lighting is not queryable or deterministic, so the sim needs its own light model.
## What
As a thief, I want shadows to genuinely hide me so that extinguishing a torch is a meaningful choice.

A sim-side light model: light emitters (point/spot/directional/ambient zones) with intensity, radius, falloff, cone; baked static occlusion (per-emitter visibility probes or cell occlusion) plus dynamic occluders (doors, large objects). lightLevel(pos) returns 0..1 with per-emitter contributions; fires and spells register emitters automatically. Includes a render-parity check.
## Scope
- In: Emitter component, ambient zones (moonlight, indoor dark), sampling API with contributions
- In: Occlusion: static bake from greybox geometry + dynamic door/large-object occluders
- In: Burning entities and light stimuli auto-register emitters
- Out: Visibility scoring — see e09-visibility-model
- Out: Light sources gameplay (extinguish/ignite) — see e03-light-sources
- Out: Beams/mirrors — see e03-light-beams
## Notes
Cache sampling in a coarse light grid (1 m) with dirty-region invalidation when emitters change. Render parity: sample positions compared against renderer luminance in Playwright to keep sim and visuals roughly aligned.

**Integration note:** Promoted to P0/m1 — e09-visibility-model (m1 AI fight) reads light level from it.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a point light of intensity 1.0 and radius 8 m, when sampled at 0, 4 and 8 m with no occluders, then values follow the documented falloff (1.0, 0.25±0.01, 0.0).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a wall between emitter and sample point, when sampled, then that emitter contributes 0.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a door that closes between an emitter and a room, when the door state changes, then samples in the room update on the next tick.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an entity starts burning, when sampled nearby, then its light contribution appears without any manual registration; when it stops burning it disappears.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a sample position outside all baked regions, when queried, then the ambient zone default is returned rather than an error (edge).
- AC-6 [perf] Given 64 dynamic emitters and 500 samples per tick, when running, then light sampling ≤ 0.5 ms per tick p95 on the reference machine.
- AC-7 [e2e] Given the greybox lighting room, when the Playwright parity probe samples 20 points, then sim light level and rendered luminance rank-correlate ≥ 0.8.

items.title: Extinguish and relight torches, candles and braziers systemically
items.description:
## Why
"Extinguishing lights" is a named thief verb; relighting a brazier is a named puzzle pattern. Both must work via properties so a water arrow, a gust, a hand pinch or rain all work.
## What
As a thief, I want to snuff torches by hand, with a water arrow, or with a gust so that I can carve a path through darkness.

Light source prefabs (candle, torch, wall sconce, brazier, lantern, fireplace) = flammable fuel + light emitter tied to burning. Extinguish via wetness, force above windResistance, smother interaction (hand, requires reach), or fuel exhaustion. Relight via heat. Enemies noticing lights out is AI's job but a lightChanged event with attribution is emitted.
## Scope
- In: Light source prefabs, snuff interaction (silent, 1.0 s), wind/force extinguish thresholds
- In: lightChanged event with source attribution
- In: Unlit-at-start and infinite-fuel flags for designers
- Out: Guard relighting behaviour — see mw-e11
- Out: Water arrows — see mw-e05
## Notes
Lanterns carried by guards are the same prefab attached to an actor — freeze or soak one and the guard walks in darkness.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given any lit light source, when its wetness rises ≥ 0.5 from any water stimulus, then it extinguishes and the local light level drops accordingly.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a candle (windResistance low) and a brazier (high), when the same force stimulus hits both, then the candle extinguishes and the brazier does not.
