- AC-3 [unit] Given a player uses snuff on a torch, when completed, then it extinguishes and emits a noise event of loudness ≤ 0.05.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an unlit torch, when any heat stimulus exceeds its ignition point, then it relights and emits lightChanged with the heat source as attribution.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a soaked torch (wetness 1.0), when heat is applied, then it does not relight until dried below 0.5 (edge).

items.title: Redirect light beams with mirrors and lenses onto receivers
items.description:
## Why
"Redirecting light" is the first puzzle example in the constitution; beams should also interact with properties (burn through webs, blind creatures, melt ice).
## What
As a player, I want to angle mirrors so that a sunbeam reaches a sealed door's sensor.

Beam emitters (sunlight shaft, crystal, spell) cast deterministic segmented rays in sim; surfaces with reflective bounce, transparent pass (with tint), opaque stop; lens focus multiplies intensity; beams apply a continuous light stimulus (and heat when focused) where they end; light receivers emit signals when intensity ≥ threshold for a dwell time.
## Scope
- In: Beam tracing with max bounces (default 8), reflection, transmission, stop
- In: Light receiver component with threshold + dwell + optional colour filter
- In: Focused beams apply heat stimulus
- Out: Rotating mirrors — see e02-push-pull (rotate affordance)
- Out: Beam VFX — see e03-state-feedback-bridge / e29-vfx-framework
## Notes
Frozen water/ice is transparent; a player or creature standing in the beam blocks it (actors are opaque) — enabling "stand here to break the beam" solutions.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a beam hitting a reflective surface at 30°, when traced, then it reflects at 30° about the surface normal within 0.01°.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a beam reaching a receiver with threshold 0.5 for dwell 1.0 s, when intensity is 0.6 for 1.0 s, then it emits activated; interrupted at 0.9 s, it does not.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a beam passing through a lens, when it hits a flammable entity, then heat stimulus is applied and the entity ignites per fire rules.
- AC-4 [unit] Given two mirrors facing each other creating a loop, when traced, then tracing stops at max bounces without hanging (edge).
- AC-5 [unit] Given an actor steps into the beam path, when traced, then the beam terminates at the actor and downstream receivers deactivate.

items.title: Build doors, locks, levers and buttons as data-wired mechanisms
items.description:
## Why
The grey-box vertical slice needs room → corridor progression; the locked-tower example needs locks that thieves pick, knights break, sorcerers bypass and keys open.
## What
As a player, I want doors that open, lock, jam, break and burn so that there is always more than one way through.

Mechanism components: door (hinged/sliding/portcullis/trapdoor, open/closed/locked/jammed/broken, speed, blocks light/gas/sound when closed), lock (tier, key id, pickable tier, magical seal flag), lever/button/crank/wheel (toggle, momentary, multi-position). All are signal emitters/receivers wired via e03-triggers. Doors are also breakables/flammables via properties (a wooden door burns; an iron door does not).
## Scope
- In: Door, lock, lever, button, crank components and state machines
- In: Lock resolution: key in inventory, lockpick capability hook, break, magical unlock hook
- In: Door as field/light/sound blocker; blocked-by-object handling
- In: Greybox prefabs for each
- Out: Lockpicking minigame — see mw-e10
- Out: Pressure plates — see e03-pressure-plates
- Out: Shootable targets — see e03-shootable-mechanisms
## Notes
Key check reads e17-inventory-core. Doors opening/closing emit noise events and update light/gas occlusion. Portcullis falling onto a crate is stopped (object weight vs. crush force) — a creative way to wedge it open.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a locked door and a player holding the matching key id, when Unlock is used, then state becomes unlocked and an unlocked event with the player as source fires.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a hinged door opening into a crate, when the door opens, then it stops at the obstruction without penetrating and emits blocked; removing the crate lets it finish.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a lever wired to a portcullis, when the lever toggles, then the portcullis receives the signal and moves at its configured speed; toggling mid-motion reverses it.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a wooden door (flammable) that burns out, when resolved, then the door becomes broken/open and no longer blocks light, gas or sound.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a portcullis closing onto an object with crush resistance above the portcullis force, when resolved, then the portcullis stops above the object (wedged) (edge).
- AC-6 [unit] Given a frozen lever, when interacted with, then it does not move and emits jammed until thawed.
- AC-7 [e2e] Given the greybox slice room, when the bot pulls a lever then walks through the opened door, then it reaches the corridor with no console errors.

items.title: Activate pressure plates by total weight of anything resting on them
items.description:
## Why
"Weighing pressure plates" is a named puzzle pattern. Plates must count any weight — crates, bodies, ice blocks, summoned skeletons — so solutions multiply.
## What
As a player, I want a plate to trigger when enough weight rests on it so that I can use a crate, a body, a frozen block or myself.

Plate component: min/max weight window, hysteresis, momentary vs latching, arming delay; weight = sum of weight properties of bodies and actors in contact (including carried items).
## Scope
- In: Plate weight summation from contacts incl. actors and their carried/equipped weight
- In: Windowed thresholds (too heavy also fails), hysteresis, latching, delay
- In: Trap variant: hidden plate outputs to trap signals
- Out: Trap effects — see mw-e10
## Notes
Weight window enables "exactly 40 kg" scale puzzles. Levitated objects (gravity scale 0) weigh nothing on a plate — emergent sorcerer trick.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a plate with min 40 kg, when a 25 kg crate and a 20 kg barrel rest on it, then it activates; removing the barrel deactivates it after hysteresis.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a plate with window 40–60 kg, when 70 kg rests on it, then it does not activate (too heavy).
- AC-3 [unit] Given an actor carrying a 10 kg object stands on a plate, when summed, then weight includes actor + carried weight.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an object under gravity-scale 0 (levitated) hovers touching the plate, when summed, then it contributes 0 kg (edge).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a latching plate, when weight is removed after activation, then it stays active until reset by a signal.

items.title: Trigger distant mechanisms with projectiles, impacts and force
items.description:
## Why
"The archer might shoot a distant mechanism." Bullseye switches, bells, hanging counterweights and crystal switches must respond to any impact source, so thrown rocks and spells work too.
## What
As an archer, I want to shoot a target on a far wall to lower a bridge so that precision opens routes others must work around.

Impact-switch component: activates when an impact/stimulus meets its filter (min energy, damage type set, element set, hit zone). Variants: bullseye (pierce, small hit zone), bell (any impact, emits loud noise), crystal (charge/light), counterweight (release via rope support).
## Scope
- In: Impact switch with filters and hit-zone geometry
- In: Variants as prefabs; bell as noise-emitting distraction tool
- In: Outputs to signal system
- Out: Arrow projectile — see e05-bow-core
## Notes
A sorcerer's Mage Hand pressing the button, a thief's thrown dagger, a knight's thrown shield — all valid if the filter permits. Designers restrict filters only deliberately.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a bullseye filtered to pierce with min energy 20 J, when a 25 J pierce impact hits inside the hit zone, then it activates; the same impact 5 cm outside the zone does not.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a bell switch filtered to any impact, when a thrown object at ≥ 5 J hits it, then it activates and emits a noise event with loudness 1.0.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a crystal switch filtered to charge, when a heat stimulus hits it, then it does not activate; a charge stimulus does.
- AC-4 [unit] Given multiple hits in one tick on a momentary switch, when resolved, then exactly one activation event fires (edge).

items.title: Wire trigger volumes and mechanisms with data-defined signal graphs
items.description:
## Why
Designers must connect levers to doors and volumes to events without writing code (fast content creation, reusable interaction systems).
## What
As a designer, I want to connect a trigger volume or lever to any receiver in data so that I can build encounters and mechanisms without scripts.

Signal graph: emitters (trigger volumes with filters — actor tag, property predicate, weight, element presence; levers; plates; receivers) → wires → receivers (doors, lights, spawners, audio cues, world-fact setters). Logic nodes: AND, OR, NOT, XOR, timer/delay, pulse, latch, counter, sequence (ordered inputs), random (seeded). Evaluated deterministically once per tick in topological order with cycle detection.
## Scope
- In: Trigger volume component with enter/exit/stay and property-predicate filters
- In: Signal graph schema (zod), runtime evaluation, logic node library
- In: Validator: missing targets, cycles without delay, unused outputs
- Out: Puzzle goal evaluation — see e15-puzzle-kit
- Out: World-fact persistence — see e27-world-state-store (receiver provided there)
## Notes
Filters are property predicates ("any entity with burning=true enters"), never type ids. Cycles are allowed only through delay/latch nodes to avoid same-tick oscillation.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a trigger volume filtered to entities with burning=true, when a burning object enters, then enter fires; a non-burning player entering does not fire it.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an AND node with two lever inputs, when only one lever is on, then output is off; when both are on, output is on on the same tick.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a sequence node expecting inputs A,B,C, when inputs arrive A,C,B, then it resets and emits a failed pulse; A,B,C emits success.
- AC-4 [content] Given a signal graph with a zero-delay cycle, when validated, then validation fails naming the cycle nodes (edge).
- AC-5 [content] Given a wire referencing a missing entity id, when validated, then validation fails with the file path and id.
- AC-6 [unit] Given the same graph and inputs, when evaluated on two runs, then emitted signal order is identical.

items.title: Mark climbable surfaces and ledges from properties and geometry
items.description:
## Why
Climbing routes must be authorable quickly and change systemically (burn ivy, freeze a wall, prop a ladder).
## What
As a designer, I want to tag surfaces as climbable and have ledges auto-detected so that I can create alternate routes quickly.

Climbable property on colliders with grade (ladder, rope, ivy, rough, sheer=no), plus an offline/at-load ledge extraction pass over greybox geometry producing ledge segments (with overrides to disable/enable). Property changes at runtime (ivy burned, surface frozen → slippery) update climbability.
## Scope
- In: Climbable grade property + capability requirement data
- In: Ledge extraction pass with per-edge override markup, ledge query API
- In: Runtime invalidation on property change
- Out: Player climbing movement — see e02-climb-surfaces, e02-ledge-mantle
## Notes
Ivy uses material ivy (flammable) — burning removes the climbable property via burnt-state data. Frozen surfaces set a slippery flag that blocks climbing unless the actor has ice tools (future).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a greybox box of height 1.5 m, when ledge extraction runs, then ledge segments are produced along its top edges and none along vertical edges.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an edge override disable, when extraction runs, then no ledge is produced there.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an ivy surface that burns out, when the burnt state applies, then its climbable grade becomes none and ledge/climb queries reflect it on the next tick.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a surface becomes frozen, when queried, then climbable returns slippery and climb attach is refused (edge).
- AC-5 [content] Given a level file with a climbable grade not in the enum, when validated, then validation fails.

items.title: Hide in wardrobes, barrels and haystacks and search containers
items.description:
## Why
Hiding places are a named stealth factor; containers hold loot, bodies and secrets. They must also be systemic (a burning haystack evicts you; a searched wardrobe is found).
## What
As a thief, I want to slip into a wardrobe or haystack and stash bodies in chests so that I can break line of sight and cover my tracks.

Hideable component (capacity, concealment 0..1, exit points, noise on enter/exit, peek allowed) and container component (inventory, lockable via e03 lock, capacity by weight, holds bodies if large). Actors inside are removed from sight queries except by search; containers that burn/break eject contents and occupants.
## Scope
- In: Enter/exit hide verbs via interaction, peek camera hook, occupancy
- In: Container inventory binding to e17, open/search/loot affordances
- In: Break/burn/submerge ejects occupants and spills contents
- Out: AI searching hiding spots — see mw-e11 (uses the occupancy query)
- Out: Loot tables — see e18-loot-tables
## Notes
Hay is flammable; hiding in a haystack next to a torch-wielding guard is a story. Occupancy query: isOccupied(entity) for AI search, respecting "last seen near" logic on their side.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a hideable with capacity 1, when the player enters, then the player is flagged hidden with the container concealment value and a second actor cannot enter.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a hidden player, when the hideable ignites or breaks, then the player is ejected to the nearest free exit point on that tick and takes heat exposure if burning.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a container holding items, when it breaks, then all items spawn as world pickups around it.
- AC-4 [unit] Given all exit points are blocked, when the player tries to exit, then exit is refused and the prompt shows "Blocked" (edge).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a container with capacity 60 kg, when a 70 kg body is stashed, then it is refused.
- AC-6 [integration] Given the save system, when saving with an item and a body inside a chest, then after reload both are still inside (via e27).

items.title: Apply world properties and elements to creatures and the player
items.description:
## Why
Enemies are part of the same world: a soaked goblin conducts lightning, a burning spider flees, a knight in iron armor is conductive, a frozen skeleton shatters. No per-creature element scripts.
## What
As a sorcerer, I want creatures to be wet, burning, frozen or charged by the same rules as objects so that combining spells on enemies is intuitive.

Actors carry the same property components (with actor-specific resistances from e12 creature data and equipment): wetness, temperature, burning, frozen (slow → immobilised), charge, conductive (from armor), weight (for plates/carry). Element rules emit actor-facing events (onFire, frozenSolid, shocked, soaked) that combat/AI respond to. Actors spread fire to what they touch.
## Scope
- In: Property components on actors with resistance modifiers from creature/equipment data
- In: Status thresholds and events; movement speed modifier hooks
- In: Burning actors ignite flammables they touch; wet actors extinguish
- Out: Damage values and poise — see e04-damage-model
- Out: AI panic/flee — see mw-e11
- Out: Creature data schema — see e12-creature-schema
## Notes
Frozen-solid actors become temporary physics objects with fragile=true (the shatter combo) — pushing one off a ledge should work.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given any actor with wetness ≥ 0.5, when a charge stimulus hits it, then shock intensity is multiplied by the conductive-wet factor from data.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a burning actor moving through flammable grass cells, when ticks run, then grass cells along its path ignite.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an actor accumulating cold beyond its frozen threshold, when resolved, then it becomes frozen solid (immobile, fragile) for the data duration and emits frozenSolid.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an actor with fire immunity (resistance 1.0), when exposed to heat, then burning never becomes true but it can still ignite things it touches if its own burning is data-forced (e.g. fire elemental) (edge).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a player equips iron armor, when conductive is queried, then it returns true; unequipping restores the base value.

items.title: Emit noise events from world interactions with material loudness
items.description:
## Why
Breaking glass, slamming doors, falling crates, bells and splashes must be audible to AI and audio through one consistent event, not per-system hacks.
## What
World systems (impacts, breaks, doors, mechanisms, splashes, fire crackle, explosions) emit NoiseEvent{pos, loudness, kind, source} via the event bus, with loudness computed from impact energy × material loudness (data).
## Scope
- In: NoiseEvent type + emission from e03 systems
- In: Material loudness data, energy→loudness curve
- Out: Propagation, occlusion and perception — see e09-sound-propagation, e11-perception
- Out: Audio playback — see e28-audio-engine
## Notes
Related: e09-sound-propagation consumes these; keep the event schema stable and documented in docs/design/noise-events.md.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a crate impact of 200 J on stone, when resolved, then a NoiseEvent is emitted with loudness from the documented curve and the impact source.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a door slam vs a slow close, when compared, then slam loudness ≥ 3× slow close loudness.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 50 micro-impacts per second from a settling pile below the min energy threshold, when resolved, then no noise events are emitted (edge: spam suppression).

items.title: Property-test all element × property combinations in a matrix harness
items.description:
## Why
Emergence is only a feature if it is safe: combinations nobody designed must not crash, loop forever or break invariants. Property-based testing is how we cover a combinatorial space we cannot enumerate by hand.
## What
As a developer, I want a generator-driven harness that throws random entities (random property sets) and random stimulus sequences into a sandbox world so that invariants hold for every element × property combination.

Uses fast-check to generate property bags and stimulus programs; runs N ticks headless; checks invariants: determinism (double-run hash), termination (fields return to ambient after sources stop), conservation (heat/gas/water within tolerance), no NaN/Infinity, state consistency (frozen ⇒ not burning; burnt ⇒ fuel 0), no type-pair logic reachable. Emits a matrix report (element × property → observed transitions) committed as docs/design/interaction-matrix.md.
## Scope
- In: fast-check arbitraries for property bags, materials and stimulus programs
- In: Invariant library and shrinking-friendly failure output (seed + minimal case)
- In: Matrix report generator; CI job with fixed seed budget ≤ 60 s + nightly long run
- Out: Handcrafted scenario replays — see e03-emergence-scenarios
## Notes
Every failing case found becomes a named regression test. Matrix report diff in PRs makes emergent behaviour changes visible to designers ("this PR makes wet wood no longer conduct").
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 500 generated worlds × 300 ticks with a fixed seed, when run in CI, then all invariants hold and the job completes in ≤ 60 s.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a deliberately injected bug (burning allowed while frozen), when the harness runs, then it fails and prints a shrunk minimal reproduction with seed.
- AC-3 [unit] Given every pair of (element ∈ heat,cold,water,charge,force,gas,light) × (property ∈ schema), when the matrix report is generated, then every cell is populated with observed transitions or "no effect".
- AC-4 [integration] Given a PR that changes an element rule, when CI runs, then the regenerated matrix report is diffed and the diff is attached to the job summary.
- AC-5 [unit] Given extreme values (temperature 1e6, weight 0, radius 0), when generated, then no NaN/Infinity appears in any property or field cell (edge).

items.title: Replay a library of emergent combo scenarios in a greybox chaos room
items.description:
## Why
We need living proof that "Wait… I can do that?" moments emerge from properties, and a regression net so they keep emerging as rules change.
## What
As a designer, I want a catalogue of emergent combos, each a replayable greybox scenario, so that I can see and protect the game's surprising interactions.

A chaos-room greybox level plus ≥ 12 scenario files, each with setup, input log and asserted outcome expressed via properties/facts. Initial catalogue: oil puddle ignition chain; burn rope → dropped chandelier; freeze river → walk across; soak enemies + charge in puddle; frozen actor shattered by blunt hit; levitated crate weighs 0 on plate; wedge portcullis with crate; gust extinguishes candles but not brazier; smoke blocks sight line; burning haystack ejects hider; focused beam ignites web barrier; ice block on pressure plate melts → plate releases (timer puzzle for free).
## Scope
- In: Chaos room level, scenario schema, runner integrated with e00-replay-harness
- In: 12+ scenarios with property-based outcome assertions
- In: Catalogue doc docs/design/emergence-catalogue.md generated from scenario metadata
- Out: Randomised coverage — see e03-interaction-matrix
## Notes
Scenario outcomes are phrased as properties ("some entity with flammable ends burnt"), never "the rope entity". New combos discovered in playtests get added here.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given each scenario, when replayed in CI, then the asserted property outcome holds and the final state hash matches its golden.
- AC-2 [content] Given the scenario directory, when validated, then there are ≥ 12 scenarios and each has setup, inputs, outcome and a player-facing description.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a rule change breaks a scenario, when CI runs, then the failure names the scenario and its outcome description.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the ice-on-plate scenario, when simulated, then the plate deactivates only after the ice melts below the weight threshold (edge: time-based emergent state).
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the chaos room in the browser, when the Playwright bot runs the rope/chandelier scenario, then it completes with no console errors.

items.title: Show burning, wet, frozen and charged states through VFX and audio
items.description:
## Why
Systems the player cannot read are systems the player cannot exploit. Wet, frozen, charged and burning must be legible at a glance.
## What
As a player, I want to see and hear that something is soaked, frozen or crackling with charge so that I can plan combos.

A presentation bridge subscribing to propertyChanged and element events: drives material parameters (wet darkening, frost overlay, char), VFX hooks (fire, steam, sparks, smoke volumes, beams) via e29 and audio cues (crackle loops, sizzle, freeze crack, zap) via e28. Placeholder grey-box visuals are acceptable; final art via separate beads.
## Scope
- In: Event → material/VFX/audio mapping table in data
- In: Pooling and LOD for element VFX; field-visualisation for gas/smoke
- In: Playwright smoke + perf checks
- Out: Final VFX art — see mw-e29 asset beads
- Out: Final SFX — see mw-e38 asset beads
## Notes
Mapping is data-driven by property/state, not entity type: any burning entity gets fire VFX sized to its bounds.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the mapping table, when an entity gains burning=true, then exactly one fire VFX handle is requested sized to its bounds and released when burning=false.
- AC-2 [unit] Given 200 entities ignite in one tick, when bridged, then VFX requests beyond the pool cap (64) are LOD-culled by distance deterministically (edge).
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the chaos room, when the fire and freeze scenarios run in the browser, then VFX nodes appear (scene probe) and there are no console errors.
- AC-4 [perf] Given 40 burning entities and a smoke cloud in view, when rendering on the reference machine (High), then frame time p95 ≤ 16.7 ms.
- AC-5 [manual] Given a playtest, when testers are shown 6 objects in different states, then ≥ 80% correctly identify wet, frozen, burning and charged without UI text.

items.title: Show properties, element fields and light levels in a debug overlay
items.description:
## Why
Designers and developers cannot tune invisible fields. Developer tooling is a technical pillar.
## What
Debug overlay (via e33 debug console) toggling: property inspector on the focused entity (with live edit), temperature/moisture/gas/charge heatmaps, light level grid, signal-graph wire view with live states, stimulus log timeline. Console commands to spawn stimuli (stim heat 500 r=2 at cursor).
## Scope
- In: Overlay layers + inspector panel + console commands
- In: Read-only in production builds (stripped)
- Out: Puzzle inspector — see e15-puzzle-inspector
## Notes
Overlay reads sim state through the public query API only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the overlay toggled to temperature, when a heat stimulus is spawned, then the heatmap shows the hot region within 1 frame.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the inspector on an entity, when wetness is edited to 1.0, then the sim reflects it next tick and propertyChanged fires.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a production build, when scanned, then overlay code is absent (edge).
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed, when the overlay is toggled through all layers, then no console errors occur.

items.title: Budget element, physics and light simulation cost per tick
items.description:
## Why
Systemic worlds die by a thousand cuts in the browser. The element sim must stay within a fixed slice of the frame on the reference and low-preset machines.
## What
Stress scenes (large fire spread, flooded room freezing, gas explosion, 200 physics bodies) with perf assertions wired into e32. Add adaptive degradation: when budget exceeded, reduce far-chunk update rate deterministically (sim-rate LOD keyed by distance, not by wall time, to keep determinism).
## Scope
- In: 4 stress scenes + perf tests
- In: Deterministic distance-based update LOD for field chunks
- Out: Global frame budget — see e32-perf-budgets
## Notes
LOD must not depend on measured frame time (non-deterministic); only on player distance and active counts.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the fire-spread stress scene (2,000 active cells), when simulated on the reference machine, then element step ≤ 2.0 ms per tick p95.
- AC-2 [perf] Given the same scene on the low-preset profile, when simulated, then element step ≤ 3.5 ms per tick p95.
- AC-3 [unit] Given field chunks > 40 m from the player, when LOD applies, then they update every 4th tick and results are deterministic across runs.
- AC-4 [perf] Given the gas explosion scene (worst case), when simulated, then no single tick exceeds 8 ms (edge: spike).

items.title: Define the puzzle data schema with goals, solutions and policies
items.description:
## Why
Puzzles are data, not code (contract §1). A schema is the contract between designers, the runtime and the validator.
## What
A zod schema for content/puzzles/*.json: id, region, entity refs (by level entity id), goal condition (expression over live properties and world facts), declared solutions (name, required capability set, abstract step list for the validator), reset policy, hint ladder, tags (mvp, class focus), and rewards/fact outputs.
## Scope
- In: Schema + example puzzle + schema tests
- In: Cross-reference validation against level entity ids
- Out: Runtime evaluation — see e15-puzzle-kit
- Out: Goal expression language — see e15-goal-conditions
## Notes
Capability sets reference e19 capability ids (e.g. spell.frost, arrow.rope, climb.rough). Related: e19-progression-core defines capability ids.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the example puzzle file, when validated, then it passes and every field is documented.
- AC-2 [content] Given a puzzle referencing an entity id absent from its level, when validated, then validation fails naming the id and level.
- AC-3 [content] Given a puzzle tagged mvp with fewer than 2 declared solutions, when validated, then validation fails (edge).
- AC-4 [content] Given a solution requiring an unknown capability id, when validated, then validation fails with the id.

items.title: Express puzzle goals as conditions over live properties and facts
items.description:
## Why
Puzzle goals must describe outcomes ("all braziers lit", "a beam reaches the sensor", "≥ 40 kg on the plate") rather than steps, so any method that achieves the outcome counts.
## What
As a designer, I want to write goals like all(entities tagged brazier-3, burning) so that any way of lighting them solves the puzzle.

A small, deterministic condition language: property predicates on entity refs or tag sets (all/any/count ≥ n), signal state, world facts (via e27 queries), spatial predicates (entity inside volume), boolean combinators, and sustained-for duration. Compiled once to a closure; evaluated each tick only when dependencies change.
## Scope
- In: Grammar/JSON AST + compiler + dependency tracking
- In: Predicates: property, signal, fact, inVolume, sustained(seconds)
- In: Human-readable explain() for debug and hints
- Out: Fact store — see e27-world-state-store
## Notes
Shares the fact predicate primitives from e27-fact-queries rather than duplicating them.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given goal all(tag:brazier, burning), when 2 of 3 braziers burn, then it is false; when the third ignites by any source, then it becomes true on that tick.
- AC-2 [unit] Given goal sustained(inVolume(any weight≥40, plateZone), 3s), when weight is held for 2.9 s then removed, then it stays false.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a goal whose dependencies did not change this tick, when the runtime ticks, then the goal is not re-evaluated (dependency tracking).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a malformed goal AST (unknown predicate), when compiled, then compilation fails with a path to the node (edge).
- AC-5 [unit] Given any goal, when explain() is called, then it returns a readable string listing each sub-condition and its current truth value.

items.title: Run data-defined puzzles composed from reusable world objects
items.description:
## Why
Designers can construct systemic puzzles from reusable world objects instead of custom-coding every puzzle (E15 outcome).
## What
As a designer, I want to drop a puzzle file next to a level and have it tracked, solved, rewarded and persisted so that I never write TypeScript for a puzzle.

Puzzle runtime: loads puzzle definitions for the active level, binds entity refs, tracks lifecycle (dormant → discovered → in-progress → solved/failed), evaluates goal conditions, fires outputs (signals, world facts, rewards), detects which declared solution path was used where possible (by capability usage trail), and persists state via e27.
## Scope
- In: Lifecycle state machine and discovery triggers (volume enter / first interaction)
- In: Outputs: signal emit, fact set, reward hook, one-shot vs repeatable
- In: Solution attribution from stimulus/capability trail
- In: Designer guide docs/design/puzzles.md
- Out: Prefab pieces — see e15-prefab-pieces
- Out: Validation tooling — see e15-solvability-validator
## Notes
Unanticipated solutions are welcome: if the goal becomes true via an undeclared route, attribution records "undeclared" and emits a telemetry event — valuable designer feedback.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a puzzle in dormant state, when the player enters its discovery volume, then it becomes discovered and emits puzzleDiscovered.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an in-progress puzzle, when its goal becomes true, then it becomes solved, emits configured signals and sets its solved fact exactly once.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a solved one-shot puzzle, when its goal later becomes false (e.g. brazier extinguished), then it remains solved and outputs are not re-fired.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the goal was reached using capabilities not matching any declared solution, when solved, then attribution = undeclared and a puzzleSolvedUndeclared event fires (edge).
- AC-5 [integration] Given a solved puzzle, when saved and reloaded, then it is still solved and its outputs (door open) are restored without re-firing rewards.
- AC-6 [integration] Given the greybox brazier puzzle, when the bot lights all braziers with a torch in one replay and a fire stimulus from range in another, then both replays solve it.

items.title: Ship reusable puzzle prefabs built only from world components
items.description:
## Why
Fast content creation: designers compose from a kit rather than asking engineers for "a mirror that turns".
## What
As a designer, I want a palette of puzzle prefabs so that I can assemble puzzles in minutes.

Prefabs (data only, composed from e03 components): rotatable statue (facing sensor), rotatable mirror, lens stand, weighted crate set (5/10/20/40 kg), brazier (flammable + receiver), water basin with valve and drain, counterweight lift, sliding block (grid pushable), bell, crystal receiver, beam sensor, scale plate pair, timed door, rune tile (sequence input).
## Scope
- In: 15 prefabs + per-prefab tests exercising their property behaviour
- In: Prefab catalogue docs generated from data
- Out: Final models/art — see mw-e37 asset beads
## Notes
Rule: a prefab may not introduce a new TypeScript component. If one is needed, it goes to e03 first as a general property/component.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given each prefab, when validated, then it references only existing e03 components and passes schema.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the rotatable statue prefab facing north, when rotated 4 steps, then its facing sensor emits the facing value east/south/west/north in order.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the basin prefab with valve opened, when simulated, then water level drops and a submerged plate at its bottom becomes reachable.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a prefab instance with a required override missing (e.g. mirror without step angle), when loaded, then default values apply or validation fails if no default exists (edge).
- AC-5 [content] Given the prefab directory, when the docs generator runs, then docs/design/puzzle-prefabs.md lists all prefabs with their properties and outputs.

items.title: Support ordered, timed and sound-clue puzzle mechanisms
items.description:
## Why
"Following sounds" and "interpreting books" are named puzzle types; ordered/timed mechanisms generalise bell towers, rune floors and race-the-door puzzles.
## What
As a player, I want to hear chimes behind a wall and replay their order on bells so that listening and observation are puzzle skills.

Prefab-level wiring using e03 logic nodes: sound-clue emitters (play a sequence of positional cues on trigger), sequence validators with tolerance, timed windows (open door for N seconds after plate), and book-clue binding (a readable item text references puzzle ids for hint attribution).
## Scope
- In: Sound clue emitter component (cue list, spacing, positional audio via e28)
- In: Sequence + timed window prefab compositions
- In: Readable clue binding for attribution
- Out: Book reading UI — see mw-e17 / mw-e07
## Notes
Accessibility: every sound clue has a subtitle/visual equivalent (E31) — e.g. subtitle "[high chime, left]".
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a sound clue emitter with cues [low, high, mid], when triggered, then three cue events fire in order at the configured spacing (1.0 s).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a sequence validator expecting [low, high, mid], when the player strikes bells low, high, mid, then success fires; any wrong bell resets and fires a failure cue.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a timed door of 8 s, when the plate is released and the player passes at 8.1 s, then the door is closed.
- AC-4 [unit] Given subtitles enabled, when a clue cue fires, then a subtitle event with its direction label is emitted (edge: accessibility).

items.title: Prove declared puzzle solutions reachable with a headless solver
items.description:
## Why
Multiple solutions must be verified, not hoped for. A headless solver catches broken puzzles before playtests do.
## What
As a designer, I want to run a validator that proves each declared solution works for its capability set so that I know my puzzle is solvable before anyone plays it.

Two layers: (1) abstract search — a BFS/A* over an abstracted puzzle state (mechanism states, object cells, element states) with actions derived from the capability set (push, rotate, ignite, freeze, levitate, shoot, climb), proving the goal reachable within a step bound; (2) concrete confirmation — each declared step list is executed in the headless sim with scripted actions to confirm the goal. Reports unreachable solutions, minimum steps, and shortcut solutions found with fewer capabilities.
## Scope
- In: Abstract state extraction from puzzle + level data
- In: Capability → action generators; bounded search with memoisation
- In: Headless concrete execution of declared step lists via e00-replay-harness
- In: CLI: pnpm puzzle:validate [id] + CI job
- Out: Softlock detection — see e15-softlock-guard
- Out: Class coverage report — see e15-solution-audit
## Notes
Abstraction must be conservative; when the abstract solver says unreachable but the concrete run succeeds, report an abstraction gap. Time-box per puzzle 10 s in CI.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a brazier puzzle with a declared solution requiring spell.fire, when validated, then the solver finds a path and reports minimum step count.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a puzzle whose only declared solution needs a crate that the level does not contain, when validated, then it reports the solution unreachable with the missing requirement.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a puzzle solvable with an empty capability set although tagged class-specific, when validated, then it reports a shortcut solution (informational warning).
- AC-4 [integration] Given each declared step list, when executed in the headless sim, then the goal becomes true; failures show the step index where it diverged.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a state space exceeding the search bound, when validated, then it stops at the bound within 10 s and reports inconclusive rather than hanging (edge).
- AC-6 [integration] Given CI, when any mvp puzzle has an unreachable declared solution, then the job fails.

items.title: Detect puzzle softlocks and recover with diegetic resets
items.description:
## Why
Failure creates stories, not dead saves. Burning the only crate or dropping the key object into a chasm must not permanently block progress (or must be a deliberate, alternate-route design).
## What
As a player, I want puzzles to recover when I destroy or lose a key object so that experimenting never bricks my save.

Validator side: search for reachable irreversible states from which the goal is unreachable and require a declared recovery policy. Runtime side: recovery policies — respawn source (crate chute drops a new crate after N s), reset lever (restore mechanism states), reversible-only flag, or alternate route declared. Resets are diegetic and persisted.
## Scope
- In: Softlock search extension to the solver (irreversible transitions: burn, break, fall out of bounds, melt)
- In: Runtime policies: respawner, reset lever/volume, out-of-bounds return
- In: Reset fact + telemetry event
- Out: Save rollback — out of scope; recovery is in-world
## Notes
Objects falling out of the world are returned to their spawner via an out-of-bounds trigger (property-based: any entity with puzzleCritical=true).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a weighted-plate puzzle whose only crate is flammable, when the solver explores burning it, then it reports a softlock unless a recovery policy exists.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a respawner policy of 10 s, when the critical crate is destroyed, then a replacement spawns at the chute after 10 s and emits puzzleRecovered.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a puzzleCritical object falls below the kill plane, when resolved, then it returns to its spawn point within 1 tick without breaking.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a reset lever, when pulled, then all mechanism states in the puzzle return to authored defaults and the puzzle state returns to in-progress (unless already solved).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a respawner whose chute is blocked by an object, when respawning, then it retries each 2 s and never spawns overlapping geometry (edge).

items.title: Report and enforce per-class solution coverage for puzzles in CI
items.description:
## Why
"Problems support multiple solutions" and "Classes change possibilities" must be measurable across the MVP.
## What
A report (docs/design/puzzle-coverage.md, regenerated in CI) listing each puzzle × {knight, archer, sorcerer, thief, any} with validated solvability, minimum capability sets and step counts. CI rule: every mvp puzzle ≥ 2 validated distinct solutions and solvable by at least 3 of 4 classes at MVP capability levels.
## Scope
- In: Class capability profiles at MVP progression milestones (data)
- In: Report generator + CI gate + PR diff summary
- Out: Encounter-level route audits — see mw-e16
## Notes
Related: mw-e16 class-specific solutions will reuse the class capability profiles; e19-progression-core supplies capability ids.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given all puzzles, when the audit runs, then the report lists every puzzle with per-class solvable yes/no/inconclusive.
- AC-2 [integration] Given an mvp puzzle solvable by only 2 classes, when CI runs, then the gate fails naming the puzzle and missing classes.
- AC-3 [unit] Given two declared solutions that reduce to the same capability set and step list, when counted, then they count as 1 distinct solution (edge).

items.title: Build greybox reference puzzles for light, freezing and weight
items.description:
## Why
The kit is only proven when real puzzles are built with zero code. These cover the first three constitution examples.
## What
As a designer, I want three reference puzzles in greybox so that the kit is proven and future designers have templates.

(1) Sunbeam: redirect light via mirrors to a sensor — also solvable by igniting a brazier near the sensor or a light spell. (2) Frozen channel: cross a water channel — freeze it, float crates, levitate across or climb the ceiling beams. (3) Scales: two plates must hold equal weight — crates, bodies, an ice block, or standing on one yourself while levitating a crate on the other.
## Scope
- In: 3 puzzle files + greybox rooms + scenario replays for each declared solution
- In: Each ≥ 2 validated solutions (target 3–4)
- Out: Final dungeon placement and art — see mw-e26
## Notes
Zero new TypeScript permitted; any engine gap discovered becomes a bead in e03/e15.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 3 puzzle files, when validated, then each passes schema and the solvability validator with ≥ 2 distinct solutions.
- AC-2 [integration] Given each declared solution, when its replay runs in CI, then the puzzle reaches solved.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the git diff of this item, when inspected by CI script, then no files under src/ are changed (data-only proof).
- AC-4 [integration] Given the scales puzzle, when the player removes weight after solving, then the puzzle stays solved (one-shot) and the door stays open (edge).
- AC-5 [manual] Given 3 playtesters, when each attempts the puzzles, then at least 2 distinct solutions are observed per puzzle across testers.

items.title: Build greybox reference puzzles for statues, darkness and sound
items.description:
## Why
Completes the six constitution puzzle archetypes, exercising statues, darkness navigation and sound following.
## What
As a designer, I want three more reference puzzles so that all six constitution examples are proven.

(4) Watchers: rotate statues so all face the altar — push/rotate, pull remotely via levitation, or knock one over (breakable) to satisfy "no statue faces the door". (5) Dark crossing: navigate a pit room where light reveals safe tiles — torches, light spell, relighting braziers, or following the drafts in the smoke. (6) Chimes: reproduce a chime order heard behind a wall — or shoot the bells in order from a balcony, or find the order written in a book.
## Scope
- In: 3 puzzle files + greybox rooms + replays for each declared solution
- Out: Final placement — see mw-e26
## Notes
Watchers deliberately includes a destructive solution (breaking a statue) — confirm softlock policy covers it.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 3 puzzle files, when validated, then each passes with ≥ 2 distinct solutions.
- AC-2 [integration] Given each declared solution replay, when run in CI, then the puzzle reaches solved.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the Watchers puzzle, when a statue is destroyed, then the puzzle remains solvable (validator) and no softlock is reported (edge).
- AC-4 [integration] Given the git diff, when inspected, then no files under src/ change.

items.title: Offer escalating diegetic hints when players are stuck on puzzles
items.description:
## Why
Puzzles should create "aha", not abandonment. Hints must be in-world (companion remarks, glinting clues) to preserve discovery.
## What
As a player, I want subtle in-world nudges after I have been stuck a while so that I stay engaged without being handed the answer.

Hint ladder per puzzle (data): tiers triggered by time-in-puzzle and failed attempts, each tier a hint action (player bark text, highlight pulse on a relevant object, NPC rumour unlock fact). Hints are class-aware (choose a tier text relevant to current capabilities). Disable-able in settings.
## Scope
- In: Hint ladder runtime + data, class-aware selection, settings toggle
- In: Attempt counting from puzzle failure pulses
- Out: Hint UI styling — see mw-e31
## Notes
Default thresholds: tier1 at 3 min or 3 failed attempts, tier2 at 6 min, tier3 at 10 min.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a puzzle in progress for 3 min, when the tick runs, then tier-1 hint fires once and not again for that tier.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a sorcerer with spell.frost, when a tier with class variants fires, then the frost-relevant text is chosen.
- AC-3 [unit] Given hints disabled in settings, when thresholds pass, then no hint fires (edge).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a puzzle solved at 2:59, when time passes, then no hint fires.

items.title: Inspect puzzle goals, wiring and solver results in an in-game tool
items.description:
## Why
Designers iterate fastest when they can see why a puzzle is not solving (developer tooling pillar).
## What
Debug panel listing puzzles in the level with lifecycle state, live goal explain() tree, wiring graph highlight, attribution trail, and buttons to reset, force-solve, and run the solver for the current capability set.
## Scope
- In: Panel in e33 debug console; goal tree view; reset/force-solve/solve commands
- Out: Standalone level editor — out of scope
## Notes
Force-solve must set facts exactly as a real solve would (for save testing).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a level with a puzzle, when the inspector opens, then it lists the puzzle with current state and goal explain tree.
- AC-2 [integration] Given force-solve, when executed, then the solved fact and outputs match a real solve (compared via fact store diff).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the solver button on a puzzle whose search is inconclusive, when run, then the panel shows inconclusive without freezing the game for > 100 ms (runs in a worker) (edge).

items.title: Emit puzzle discovery, attempt, solve and abandon telemetry events
items.description:
## Why
E34 wants puzzle completion signals; undeclared solutions are gold for designers.
## What
Emit e34 telemetry events: puzzleDiscovered, puzzleAttemptFailed, puzzleHintShown{tier}, puzzleSolved{solutionId|undeclared, durationS, class}, puzzleAbandoned (left region > 10 min unsolved after discovery).
## Scope
- In: Event schema entries + emission from runtime
- Out: Dashboards/export — see e34-telemetry-events
## Notes
Local-first; no network by default.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a puzzle solved via an undeclared route, when solved, then puzzleSolved carries solutionId=undeclared and the capability trail.
- AC-2 [unit] Given discovery then leaving the region for 10 min unsolved, when the tick runs, then puzzleAbandoned fires once.
- AC-3 [unit] Given telemetry disabled, when events occur, then nothing is recorded (edge).

items.title: Store persistent world facts in a typed deterministic fact store
items.description:
## Why
Doors opened, characters helped, creatures befriended and treasures stolen must persist and be readable by every system (E27 outcome).
## What
As a developer, I want a single typed fact store so that quests, dialogue, puzzles and levels read and write world state consistently.

Facts are namespaced keys (global: "quest.missing-miller.stage", entity-scoped: "entity:<levelId>/<entityId>.opened") with typed values (bool, int, enum, string id, timestamp in sim ticks). API: get/set/increment/has, change events, transactional batch writes within a tick, deterministic iteration and a stable content hash for replays.
## Scope
- In: Fact store in src/sim with typed values, namespaces, change events
- In: Transaction batching per tick, deterministic hash
- In: Fact-setter receiver node for the e03 signal graph
- Out: Registry/schema of declared facts — see e27-fact-registry
- Out: Entity physical state persistence — see e27-entity-deltas
- Out: Serialization — see e27-save-integration
## Notes
Timestamps are sim ticks from the injected clock, never wall clock. Keep the store small and flat; it is not a general database.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an empty store, when set("door.cellar.opened", true) is called, then get returns true and one factChanged event fires with old=undefined/new=true.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a transaction that sets 3 facts and then throws, when rolled back, then no facts change and no events fire.
- AC-3 [unit] Given facts inserted in different orders on two runs, when hashed, then hashes are identical.
- AC-4 [unit] Given set with a value of the wrong type for an existing fact (string to bool), when called, then it throws a typed error and the value is unchanged (edge).
- AC-5 [unit] Given a signal-graph fact-setter receiver, when its input goes high, then the configured fact is set on that tick.

items.title: Declare world facts in a content registry validated at load
items.description:
## Why
Unregistered fact strings are typos waiting to break quests. A registry makes facts discoverable, typed and migratable.
## What
content/facts/*.json registry: key pattern, type, default, persistence policy (see e27-persistence-policies), description, owner system. All quest/dialogue/puzzle/level content references are cross-validated against it. Undeclared writes fail in dev/test.
## Scope
- In: Registry schema + loader + cross-reference validator for content files
- In: Dev/test strict mode: undeclared write throws; prod: logs + ignores
- Out: Quest/dialogue content — see e23-quest-runtime, e22-dialogue-runtime
## Notes
Entity-scoped fact patterns ("entity:*.opened") are declared once as templates.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the registry, when validated, then every entry has type, default and description and keys are unique.
- AC-2 [content] Given a dialogue or puzzle file referencing an undeclared fact, when validated, then validation fails naming the file and fact.
- AC-3 [unit] Given strict mode, when code writes an undeclared fact, then it throws; in production mode it logs a warning and ignores the write (edge).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a template fact "entity:*.looted", when "entity:mine/chest-3.looted" is written, then it validates against the template type.

items.title: Persist entity changes as deltas from authored level baselines
items.description:
## Why
Smashed walls, burned bridges, moved crates, looted chests and dead creatures must stay that way — without saving the entire world.
## What
As a player, I want the world to be exactly as I left it when I come back so that my actions matter.

Each level has an authored baseline. Entities flagged persistent record deltas: transform (if moved beyond epsilon and at rest), destroyed/broken, burnt state, property overrides (wetness excluded if transient), mechanism state, container contents, spawned persistent entities (dropped items, debris flagged persistent), and actor life/disposition hooks. On level load, deltas apply after baseline spawn and before first tick.
## Scope
- In: Delta capture on level unload/save, delta apply on load, spawned-entity records
- In: Per-component persistence declarations (which properties persist)
- In: Stable entity ids for authored entities; generated ids for spawned ones
- Out: Policies for transient states — see e27-persistence-policies
- Out: Actor AI state persistence — see mw-e11 (supplies its component serializer)
## Notes
Authored entity ids must be stable across level edits; the level pipeline assigns GUIDs and a lint warns if a persistent entity id disappears (orphaned delta → dropped with warning).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a crate moved 5 m and at rest, when deltas are captured, then one transform delta exists; a crate nudged 1 mm produces none.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a broken wall and a looted chest, when captured and re-applied to a fresh baseline, then the wall is broken (no collider) and the chest is empty.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a persistent dropped item spawned at runtime, when captured and re-applied, then it exists at the same position with the same item id.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a delta referencing an entity id no longer present in the level baseline, when applied, then it is skipped with a warning and loading continues (edge).
- AC-5 [integration] Given the greybox slice, when the player burns a rope bridge, leaves the level and returns, then the bridge is still gone and replay hashes match.
- AC-6 [perf] Given 5,000 deltas, when applied on level load, then application takes ≤ 30 ms on the reference machine.

items.title: Serialize world facts and entity deltas through the save system
items.description:
## Why
Save-game stability is a technical pillar; world state is the largest and most fragile part of a save.
## What
As a player, I want saving and loading to restore the whole world exactly so that I can trust my progress.

Register fact store + per-level delta sets as save sections with the e30 versioned format; lazy-load deltas for unloaded levels; version and migration hooks for fact renames/removals and component persistence changes; round-trip and migration tests.
## Scope
- In: Save section providers (facts, deltas per level), schema versions, migration functions
- In: Round-trip property tests with generated fact/delta sets
- In: Corruption handling: invalid section → recover what is valid, report
- Out: Storage/IndexedDB and save slots UI — see e30-save-serialization
## Notes
Fact renames are declared in the registry (renamedFrom) so migrations are generated, not hand-written, where possible.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 1,000 randomly generated facts and deltas (fast-check), when serialized and deserialized, then the result is deep-equal and the state hash matches.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a v1 save and a registry declaring "door.cellar.open" renamedFrom "cellar_door_open", when loaded, then the migrated fact holds the old value.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a save whose delta section for one level is corrupted, when loaded, then other sections load, that level falls back to baseline and a recoverable error is reported (edge).
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the greybox slice, when the player opens a door, loots a chest, saves, closes the browser tab and reloads the save, then the door is open and the chest empty.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a save created by the previous release fixture, when loaded by the current build, then it loads without error (migration test).

items.title: Query world facts with a shared condition API for all systems
items.description:
## Why
Quests, dialogue, puzzles, shops and level variants all need "if the minotaur was befriended and the cellar is open". One predicate language avoids four inconsistent ones.
## What
As a designer, I want to write conditions like all(fact(minotaur.befriended), not(fact(cellar.sealed))) in any content file so that every system gates on world state identically.

JSON predicate AST: fact eq/neq/gt/gte/lt/lte/has, template matches (count(entity:*.looted in level mine) ≥ 3), all/any/not, compiled with dependency lists for change-driven re-evaluation.
## Scope
- In: Predicate AST schema, compiler, dependency extraction, explain()
- In: Subscription API: onConditionChanged(cond, cb)
- Out: Puzzle-specific live-property predicates — see e15-goal-conditions (extends this)
## Notes
Related: e22-dialogue-runtime and e23-quest-runtime should consume this rather than inventing their own (integration pass).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given condition all(fact(a)=true, fact(b)≥3), when a=true and b=2, then false; when b becomes 3, then onConditionChanged fires true exactly once.
- AC-2 [unit] Given count(entity:mine/*.looted) ≥ 3, when three matching facts are true, then it evaluates true.
- AC-3 [content] Given a condition referencing an undeclared fact, when validated, then it fails (via registry).
- AC-4 [unit] Given a deeply nested condition (depth 64), when compiled, then it compiles without stack overflow; depth > 64 is rejected with a clear error (edge).

items.title: Inspect, edit and diff world state from the debug console
items.description:
## Why
Testing a late-game branch should not require replaying the game. Developer tooling pillar.
## What
Debug console commands: facts.list [prefix], facts.get/set, deltas.list [level], state.diff <saveA> <saveB>, state.snapshot/restore (in-memory), plus a panel view.
## Scope
- In: Console commands and panel
- In: Diff output grouped by facts and per-level deltas
- Out: Save slot management — see e30-save-serialization
## Notes
Dev builds only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the console, when facts.set quest.x.stage 3 is executed, then the fact is set and dependent conditions re-evaluate.
- AC-2 [integration] Given two saves differing by one looted chest, when state.diff runs, then the output lists exactly that delta.
- AC-3 [integration] Given facts.set with an undeclared key, when executed, then the console reports the error without throwing (edge).

items.title: Apply permanent, rest-reset and transient persistence policies
items.description:
## Why
Not everything should persist forever: fires burn out, ice melts, respawning herbs regrow, enemy camps may restock. Policies keep the world believable and saves small.
## What
As a designer, I want to choose whether a change is permanent, resets on rest/time, or is transient so that the world feels alive without undoing player achievements.

Policies per fact/component: permanent; resetAfter(ticks) or onRest; transient (never saved: wetness, temperature, active fires by default); decaysTo(value) on reload (burning → burnt). Declared in registry/component metadata.
## Scope
- In: Policy evaluation on save capture and on load/rest
- In: Rest event hook (from inn/campfire — owner elsewhere)
- In: Defaults: element transients not saved; burning resolves to burnt on reload
- Out: Offscreen time simulation — see e27-offscreen-catchup
- Out: Resting UI — see mw-e17 / mw-e24
## Notes
Resolving "burning at save time" to burnt on reload avoids saving the element field while keeping outcome consistency (the fire would have finished anyway).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a fact with policy resetAfter(72000 ticks), when 72000 ticks pass (loaded or not), then it returns to its default.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an entity burning at save time with policy decaysTo(burnt), when loaded, then it is in burnt state and not burning.
- AC-3 [unit] Given wetness (transient), when saved and reloaded, then wetness is 0.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a looted chest with permanent policy, when the player rests 10 times, then it stays looted.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a fact declared both transient and with a reset timer (invalid combination), when the registry validates, then it fails (edge).

items.title: Spawn fact-gated entity variants so the world reacts to choices
items.description:
## Why
Helping the miller should put him back in his mill; befriending the minotaur should change the labyrinth. The world visibly reacting is what makes actions feel meaningful.
## What
As a designer, I want to mark level entities as present/absent or swapped based on world conditions so that the world changes after player choices without scripting.

Level entities may declare spawnIf/despawnIf conditions (e27-fact-queries) and variant groups (exactly one variant active, chosen by first matching condition). Evaluated on level load and on condition change when not in player view (no pop-in within camera frustum unless flagged).
## Scope
- In: spawnIf/despawnIf + variant groups in level schema
- In: Evaluation on load + deferred out-of-view swaps
- In: Interaction with deltas (a despawned entity keeps its delta)
- Out: NPC schedules — see mw-e22 / mw-e14
## Notes
Example: boarded-up door variant appears after "cellar.sealed_by_guard"; the thief can still break the boards (they are breakable).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an entity with spawnIf(fact(miller.rescued)), when the fact becomes true while the entity location is out of view, then it spawns; if in view, it waits until out of view.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a variant group of three with conditions, when multiple conditions match, then the first listed wins deterministically.
- AC-3 [content] Given a variant group where no variant has a default/fallback, when validated, then a warning lists the uncovered case.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a despawned entity with deltas, when it respawns later, then its deltas are re-applied (edge).
- AC-5 [integration] Given the greybox slice, when a fact flips, then the corresponding variant is active after save/reload.

items.title: Track object ownership and record thefts as world facts
items.description:
## Why
"Treasures stolen" must persist, and a thief's actions should have consequences (shopkeepers notice missing stock) — without a full crime system in this epic.
## What
As a thief, I want stolen goods to be tracked as stolen so that fences, witnesses and owners can react later.

Owner tag property on items/containers/areas (owner faction or NPC id); taking an owned item without permission sets a stolen flag on the item instance and a theft fact (owner, item, location, witnessed=unknown until AI resolves). Returning or buying clears it.
## Scope
- In: Ownership property on items/containers, permission predicate
- In: Stolen item flag + theft facts; clearing rules
- In: Event for witness resolution by AI
- Out: Witness detection and crime reactions — see mw-e11 / mw-e10
- Out: Fences and prices — see e20-shop-system
## Notes
Related: e17-inventory-core stores item instance flags.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an item owned by NPC Mirela and no permission, when the player takes it, then the item instance is flagged stolen and a theft fact with owner Mirela is recorded.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player buys the item or is gifted it, when transferred, then no stolen flag is set.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a stolen item returned into its owner container, when placed, then the stolen flag clears and theft fact resolves to returned.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an unowned item (owner none), when taken, then no theft fact is recorded (edge).
- AC-5 [integration] Given a theft then save/reload, when inspected, then the stolen flag and theft fact persist.

items.title: Resolve elapsed time for unloaded levels when the player returns
items.description:
## Why
Leaving a freezing spell on a river and returning a day later should find it melted; a fire should have burned out. Cheap catch-up rules preserve consistency without simulating unloaded levels.
## What
As a player, I want time to have passed in places I left so that the world feels continuous.

On level load, compute elapsed sim time since last visit and apply analytic catch-up rules per component (ice melts after X, fires resolve to burnt, doors on timers close, puzzle respawners complete, reset policies apply) instead of simulating.
## Scope
- In: Last-visited tick per level, catch-up rule registry per component
- In: Deterministic ordered application
- Out: NPC off-screen schedules — see mw-e22
## Notes
Catch-up rules are pure functions (state, elapsed) → state, 100% unit-tested.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given ice created with melt time 10 min and a return after 30 min, when the level loads, then the ice is gone and water volume restored.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a return after 1 min, when loaded, then the ice remains with proportionally reduced thickness.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a timed door open when left, when returning after its timer, then it is closed.
- AC-4 [unit] Given elapsed time is negative or zero (clock anomaly / immediate re-entry), when loaded, then no catch-up applies and no error occurs (edge).

items.title: Budget world-state save size and serialization time
items.description:
## Why
Browser saves live in IndexedDB and autosave during play; large or slow saves cause hitches and quota errors.
## What
Stress fixture with 10,000 facts + 5,000 deltas across 6 levels; perf tests for serialize/deserialize time and compressed size; autosave must not hitch the main thread (serialize off the sim tick via snapshot + worker compression).
## Scope
- In: Stress fixture, perf tests, snapshot-then-compress in a worker
- Out: IndexedDB quota handling — see e30-save-serialization
## Notes
Budgets from epic exit criteria.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [perf] Given the stress fixture, when serialized on the reference machine, then snapshot time on the main thread ≤ 50 ms and compressed size ≤ 1 MB.
- AC-2 [perf] Given autosave during 60 s of play, when measured, then no frame exceeds 33 ms due to save work.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a snapshot taken while the sim continues ticking, when compressed in the worker, then the saved state equals the state at snapshot tick (edge: no tearing).
